audit.summary:
GeoPDF georeferencing works the same way on both platforms. iOS: ContentView.handleImport -> ImportedMapWorker.preparePDF -> GeoPDFReader.bounds. It checks the Adobe /VP on the page, then on the catalog, and picks the GEO viewport with the largest BBox. Each GPTS(lat,lon) is paired with a page point BBox-start + LPTS*(BBox-end - BBox-start), and a least-squares affine (lon=ax+by+c, lat=dx+ey+f) is fitted from those pairs. The crop is the BBox. The LGIDict fallback takes the 'Layers' entry, or the first entry, then CTM x Neatline -> Projection.inverse (LL/UT/TC/LC) -> 3-parameter datum shift -> affine, with a gate of 4 or more points and RMS <= 50 m. After that comes the known-sheet table, then a 10 km square at the camera. PDFImageOverlayView places the raster through the affine, and PDFTiler inverts it one Mercator strip at a time, drawing with PDFKit draw(with:.mediaBox). Android: importPdfMapSource does a preflight (PdfRenderer integer page size; /Rotate != 0 is rejected), then GeoPdfParser (PDFBox 2.0.27). The viewport choice and LPTS mapping match iOS. For LGIDict it prefers Registration, falls back to CTM, and uses LgiProjection/LgiDatum. The same AffineFitter runs with no RMS gate -> PdfMapSource.calibrated; PdfGroundLayer warps the whole CropBox bitmap and PdfTiler works one strip at a time.

What is solid: the project memory note is stale. Android now inverse-projects LGIDict UT/TC/LC using the same Snyder TM/LCC formulas as iOS. The TM inverse agrees with Karney to under 1 mm inside the zone. Both platforms have the same datum table, read GPTS in lat,lon order, and handle the reversed-Y BBox that USGS writes. Largest-area viewport selection, prime-meridian handling and the least-squares code are the same, and PDFBox keeps full precision.

On the real samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf (a NAD83 UTM 10N PROJCS; MediaBox/CropBox [0 0 1728 2088]; Rotate 0; three viewports; no LGIDict), both platforms reject the file. Its main viewport has LPTS values slightly outside [0,1] (D1-01), so both silently fall back to a box around the camera. If that check were relaxed, both would produce the same affine: page (0,0)->(37.728854,-122.520123), (1728,2088)->(37.888180,-122.353903). The printed quad corners (37.75/37.875 N, 122.375/122.5 W) would then land 4.7-5.0 m off. The printed 1000 m UTM grid intersections would be 3.4-6.4 m off, because the fit is affine in lat/lon rather than in UTM space (D1-02). That error grows to hundreds of metres on 1:100k and 1:250k sheets.

Divergences found: iOS draws relative to the page box with /Rotate applied; this was checked on macOS PDFKit, whose drawing behaviour iOS shares. Android draws relative to the CropBox with integer page dimensions. The two platforms also choose LGIDict entries differently, and iOS ignores /Registration. Neither applies the GCS datum to Adobe GPTS, and neither recognises real LGIDict codes such as LE or NAS-E.

findings.title: The SF North sample and other USGS US Topo GeoPDFs are rejected because LPTS must be inside [0,1]; the map silently lands in a box around the camera
findings.description: I parsed the sample directly (object streams inflated). The main 'Map Layers' viewport has BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373], and Measure obj 424 has GPTS [37.73318 -122.52121 37.88898 -122.52021 37.88818 -122.35264 37.73238 -122.354], LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514], and a /Bounds with the same values. The LPTS fall slightly outside [0,1] for a legitimate reason. USGS keeps the page true-north-up at the quad centre (0.34 deg grid convergence), so the four GPTS form a UTM-aligned rectangle (542188/556923 E, 4176319/4193606 N) that is rotated against the page-aligned BBox. GDAL maps LPTS linearly and applies no range check. The 2026-09-17 hardening commit 1c023de added `(0.0...1.0).contains(normalX/Y)` on iOS and `nx !in 0.0..1.0` on Android. With that check, the main body counts as a 'malformed declared GEO' viewport of about 3.5M pt^2. The valid 'Quadrangle Location' inset (about 5,000 pt^2) cannot outrank it, so both parsers return Rejected. iOS then drops to GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds, a 10x10 km square at the camera with kind .calibratedPDF. Android returns PdfMapSource.imported, a 10 km x aspect box at the camera, and still shows the 'Imported' toast. Neither platform shows an error. The unit tests on both platforms require LPTS=1.1 to be rejected. The screenshot UI test only checks that the map became active, and it sets the device location to the PDF centre, so the fallback box looks plausible and the bug stays hidden. iOS also saves the fallback placement (PDFSessionStore.save/load), so sheets imported before a fix stay misplaced.
findings.failure_scenario: A field user imports USGS_SF_North.pdf (the repo's documented demo GeoPDF) while the map is centred on Sydney. On iOS, the SF North topo appears as a 10x10 km square centred on Sydney; on Android, as an 8.3x10 km box there. The MGRS grid then shows Sydney grid references over San Francisco terrain. If the camera happens to be at SF, the page is still squeezed into a 10 km box instead of its true 14.6 x 17.7 km extent, so the edges are misplaced by 2-4 km. Every US Topo quad with this LPTS pattern behaves the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept any finite LPTS (or a generous range such as [-0.5, 1.5]) and map it linearly against the BBox endpoints, as GDAL does. Keep the GPTS Earth-range checks and use the fit's residual and crossValidated as the sanity gate. Update the tests that assert 1.1 is malformed. When a declared-GEO PDF is rejected, show a message instead of silently using the camera fallback. Add a migration that re-parses saved sessions whose kind is calibratedPDF but which have no user-entered fiduciaries (no MGRS), on both platforms.
findings.proving_test: iOS PDFImportSmokeTests: makeRawPDF with MediaBox [0 0 1728 2088] and pageExtras containing the three /VP dicts copied verbatim from SF North (objects 420/422/424 above). Assert GeoPDFReader.bounds(from:) != nil, SW ~ (37.73238, -122.52121) and NE ~ (37.88898, -122.35264) within 1e-5, and placementAffine.apply(CGPoint(x: 916.50, y: 1076.46)) within 10 m of (37.811024, -122.431963), which is UTM 10N 550000E 4185000N. Android PdfImportHardeningInstrumentedTest: build the same /VP with PDFBox and assert GeoPdfParser.parse(...) returns 4 correspondences, with (-12.234, 56.694) paired to (37.73318, -122.52121). Both fail today.

findings.title: GeoPDF placement fits one affine in lat/lon and ignores the sheet's projection: 3-6 m off the printed UTM grid on a 7.5' quad, 150-600 m on 1:100k/1:250k, 186 m to 1.7 km on Mercator sheets
findings.description: Both platforms reduce the georeference to lon = ax+by+c, lat = dx+ey+f. The Adobe /GCS PROJCS (UTM 10N on the sample) is never read. The LGIDict CTM is exactly affine to projected metres, but it is inverse-projected at the neatline corners and then re-fitted as a lat/lon affine. The overlay, the tiler and the MGRS grid all use that lat/lon affine. For SF North (once D1-01 is fixed), the PDF->UTM affine fits the GPTS to 0.18 m, while the lat/lon affine leaves 7.9 m at every GPTS. At printed grid intersections the lat/lon affine is 3.4-6.4 m off: for example, 543000E 4177000N (PDF 84.11,136.53) comes out at (37.739272, -122.512032) against a truth of (37.739277, -122.511960), which is 6.4 m. Quad corners are 4.7-5.0 m off. Simulated error by sheet size: 15' quad 18.5 m; 30'x60' at 1:100k 148 m; 1x2 deg at 1:250k 588 m. For a Web-Mercator sheet of 1x1 deg at 37.5N, the error is 0 m at the corners and 186 m in the middle of the sheet; for 2x2 deg at 60N it is 1.7 km, and no residual check can catch it. The Adobe path has no residual gate on either platform. The iOS LGIDict path rejects RMS > 50 m, so a 1:100k/1:250k LGIDict sheet lands in the camera fallback on iOS. Android has no gate and places the same sheet with 150-600 m error, so the two platforms disagree.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports a 1:100k 30'x60' UTM GeoPDF. On Android the in-app MGRS grid lines sit about 150 m from the printed grid at the sheet edges; on iOS the sheet is not georeferenced at all when it comes via LGIDict. On an Adobe GeoPDF exported in EPSG:3857 covering 1 deg, both platforms place the sheet's middle about 186 m north/south of truth while the corners look perfect. Even on the 1:24k SF quad, the MGRS 1 km lines visibly miss the printed ticks by up to about 6 m at maximum zoom.
findings.suggested_fix: Adobe path: parse the GCS WKT/EPSG (TM/UTM, LCC, Mercator/3857, geographic). Forward-project the GPTS to metres, fit PDF->projected (exact), and store the projection alongside the affine. The overlay and both tilers should inverse-project per strip or per mesh vertex; the tilers already work per strip. LGIDict: use the CTM directly as PDF->projected and inverse-project per tile instead of re-fitting a lat/lon affine. If the CRS is unknown, fit a 2nd-order polynomial (4+ GPTS) or a TIN, and apply the same residual gate and user warning on both platforms.
findings.proving_test: After the D1-01 fix, use the SF North /VP fixture and assert that placement(84.11, 136.53) is within 1 m of (37.739277, -122.511960) and placement(916.50, 1076.46) is within 1 m of (37.811024, -122.431963). Both are 6.4 m and 3.35 m off today. Add a synthetic LGIDict fixture: /ProjectionType (UT) /Zone 10 /Hemisphere (N) /Datum (NA), with a CTM mapping a 600x400 neatline to the UTM box of 37-38N, 124-122W. Assert that both platforms georeference it and the centre is within 5 m. Today iOS returns nil (rms gate) and Android is about 590 m off at the corners.

findings.title: Adobe GPTS are always treated as WGS84 even when the /GCS datum is NAD27, ED50 or Tokyo (roughly 50-460 m error)
findings.description: Under ISO 32000-2, and in GDAL's reader, GPTS are geographic coordinates in the GEOGCS of the viewport's /GCS. Both parsers read only PRIMEM from the GCS WKT and pass GPTS lat/lon straight into the WGS84 affine. The 3-parameter DatumShift/LgiDatum machinery already exists but is used only for LGIDict. USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection GeoPDFs are georeferenced to the original map datum, often NAD27. The sample's datum is NAD83 (GRS80), which is only about 1 m from WGS84, so it happens to be unaffected. Computed errors when a datum is treated as WGS84: NAD27 at SF 93 m, NAD27 at Denver 49 m, ED50 at Berlin 107 m, Tokyo 464 m.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports a USGS historical 1:62,500 GeoPDF whose /GCS WKT is GEOGCS["GCS_North_American_1927",DATUM["D_North_American_1927",SPHEROID["Clarke_1866",...]]]. Both apps place the sheet about 50-100 m from where the MGRS grid, the GPS position and satellite imagery say it belongs. A grid reference read off the map can land in the wrong 100 m square, with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse DATUM/SPHEROID (and TOWGS84 if present) from the GCS WKT, or use the EPSG code. Map the known datums (NAD27, ED50, Tokyo, OSGB36, NTF, Pulkovo, AGD66/84) to the existing shift table and shift each GPTS before fitting. Fail closed or warn on a non-WGS84-compatible datum the app does not recognise. Share one datum-name table across the two platforms through a testdata fixture.
findings.proving_test: Fixture: Adobe /VP with GPTS around 37.8N, -122.44 and /GCS << /Type /GEOGCS /WKT (GEOGCS["GCS_North_American_1927",DATUM["D_North_American_1927",SPHEROID["Clarke_1866",6378206.4,294.9786982]],PRIMEM["Greenwich",0.0],UNIT["Degree",0.0174532925199433]]) >>. Assert that the placed centre differs from the raw GPTS centre by about 93 m, matching the NS shift (-8,160,176). Today the difference is 0 on both platforms. Put it in a shared testdata vector checked by SharedVectorsTest on Android and an XCTest on iOS.

findings.title: iOS misregisters GeoPDFs with /Rotate != 0 or a non-zero MediaBox origin, because PDFKit draw(with:.mediaBox) rotates the page and draws it relative to the box origin
findings.description: Every GeoPDF georeference (BBox+LPTS, Neatline, CTM, Registration) is in raw, unrotated PDF user space. PDFRasteriser and PDFTiler set up a context that maps raw user space onto the image or tile, then call page.draw(with: .mediaBox, to:). PDFKit's draw applies the page rotation and translates by -box.origin. I checked this with a macOS PDFKit probe, drawing a black square at user (100..110, 100..110) with the app's exact transform sequence. With MediaBox [50 50 450 350], the square came out at user 50..59 (shifted by -origin). With /Rotate 90, it came out at y 290..299 instead of 100..109. The iOS app never reads /Rotate (grep finds nothing under Calibration/). Android fails closed with a 'rotation unsupported' message, so the two platforms behave differently.
findings.failure_scenario: A user rotates a GeoPDF to landscape in Preview, which sets /Rotate 90, and imports it on iPhone. The raster is drawn rotated into an image sized for the unrotated page (partly clipped) and placed with the unrotated affine, so terrain is 90 deg off and displaced by hundreds of metres, while the MGRS grid looks authoritative. The same file on Android shows a rejection toast. Separately, a GeoPDF whose MediaBox is [18 18 630 810] (for example Ghostscript -dUseCropBox output) has every feature shifted 18 pt towards the SW: about 152 m at 1:24k and 317 m at 1:50k, in the overlay and in the baked MBTiles.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw in raw user space. Either concatenate page.transform(for: .mediaBox).inverted() before page.draw, or use cgContext.drawPDFPage(page.pageRef!), which does not apply the box/rotate transform, in both PDFRasteriser.render and PDFTiler.renderTile. Then either support /Rotate properly (display-space georef plus a rotated raster) or reject rotation != 0 with the same message and the same inherited-/Rotate handling as Android, so the platforms agree.
findings.proving_test: XCTest: makeRawPDF with MediaBox [50 50 450 350], content '0 0 0 rg 100 100 10 10 re f', and a /VP BBox [50 50 450 350] mapped to a known lat/lon box. Render PDFRasteriser.render(url:cropRect:nil) and assert the image pixel for user (105,105), i.e. (55, 350-105-50=195), is black. Today it is white, and the black lands 50 px towards the lower left. Second case: MediaBox [0 0 400 300] with /Rotate 90. Assert either that the import is rejected or that the pixel for user (105,105) is black.

findings.title: Android georeference is in raw PDF user space but PdfRenderer draws relative to the CropBox using integer page size, so cropped PDFs are shifted and A-series pages are off by up to 1 pt
findings.description: GeoPdfParser produces correspondences in raw PDFBox user space: BBox endpoints, Neatline and MediaBox corners. pdfium, which backs PdfRenderer, maps the lower-left of CropBox∩MediaBox to device (0,0) with a y-flip. PdfRenderer.Page.getWidth()/getHeight() are ints: AOSP nativeOpenPageAndGetSize reads doubles from FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndex and stores them with SetIntField, which truncates. PdfTiler.pageRectForBand treats device coordinates as (x, h_int - y) with origin 0, and PdfGroundLayer and calibratedPdfBounds use page corners (0,0)-(w_int,h_int). So any PDF whose effective CropBox lower-left is not (0,0) is shifted by that origin. A page with a fractional height (every ISO A size: A4 841.89, A3 1190.55, A1 2383.94 pt) is also off by up to frac(H) pt at one edge; depending on the pdfium build this is a shift or a scale. iOS renders the MediaBox with doubles and has neither error for CropBox-cropped files, so the platforms disagree on the same file. It does not affect the SF sample (CropBox = MediaBox = [0 0 1728 2088]).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A user trims the white margin of a GeoPDF in Acrobat or Preview, which writes CropBox [36 36 1692 2052] inside MediaBox [0 0 1728 2088], and imports it on Android. The overlay and the baked MBTiles are shifted 36 pt, about 305 m at 1:24k, while the same file on iPhone is correct. (b) An Australian 1:50k GeoPDF on A1 (height 2383.94 pt) is off by 0.94 pt north-south on Android: about 8 m at 1:25k, 17 m at 1:50k and 83 m at 1:250k against the MGRS grid.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the effective CropBox (PDFBox page.cropBox, which already clips to and defaults to the MediaBox) as doubles. Store llx, lly, width and height as Double in PdfPageInfo. Convert every correspondence and fiducial to renderer space consistently: device = ((x - llx) * Wint/W, (lly + H - y) * Hint/H), or pass an explicit transform built from the real dimensions. Use the same conversion in PdfTiler, PdfGroundLayer and calibratedPdfBounds.
findings.proving_test: androidTest: use PDFBox to create a page with MediaBox [0 0 600 400], CropBox [36 36 600 400], a filled 4x4 square at user (300,200), and an Adobe VP on BBox [0 0 600 400] with GPTS -34/150 .. -33/151. Run importPdfMapSource, then PdfTiler.generate. Decode the tile containing the lat/lon of user (302,202) at maxZoom and assert that pixel is dark; today the dark pixels sit about 36 pt (about 0.06 deg) away. Repeat with MediaBox [0 0 595.28 841.89] and a square near the top edge, and assert an error of 1 px or less.

findings.title: LGIDict code tables don't match real files: LCC is 'LE' (the apps accept 'LC') and datums such as NAS-E/NAS-C/NAR-C/WGE are rejected, so real projected LGIDict GeoPDFs fall back to the camera
findings.description: A USGS-produced LGIDict posted on the Global Mapper forum reads `/Projection << /CentralMeridian (-121.688) /Datum (NAS-E) /FalseEasting (0) /FalseNorthing (0) /OriginLatitude (46.75) /ProjectionType (LE) /StandardParallelOne (33) /StandardParallelTwo (45) /Units (M) >>`. Based on my memory of GDAL's pdfdataset.cpp, GDAL also handles 'LE' for LCC, 'WGE' for WGS84, 'NAR'/'NAR-*' for NAD83 and 'NAS'/'NAS-*' for NAD27, and possibly 'GEOGRAPHIC' for lat/lon. Both apps accept only 'LC' plus LL/UT/TC, and only the 2-letter datum codes WE/WD/GD/NA/OB/OG/OS/EU/NS/TC/CH/NT/NF/KK. Projected CRSs require an explicit understood datum, so a real file fails parseDatum or the projection switch. iOS then returns crop-only (GeoPDFReader.swift:672-675, 781-784), falls through to fallbackBounds, and marks the source calibratedPDF. Android's projectionConverter returns null, no correspondences are produced, and it uses the base camera box. Both platforms behave the same, and both do it silently.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports an NGA or legacy TerraGo GeoPDF with /ProjectionType (UT) /Zone 10 /Hemisphere (N) /Datum (WGE), or a USGS LCC quad with (LE)/(NAS-E). Both phones show the sheet as a box around the current camera, with no warning that the georeference was ignored.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept 'LE' (and keep 'LC'), and 'GEOGRAPHIC' alongside LL/LONGLAT. Add the DIGEST/OGC Annex A datum codes: WGE -> WGS84; NAR, NAR-* -> NAD83 with zero shift; NAS-C (-8,160,176), NAS-E (-10,158,187) and other NAS-* -> Clarke 1866; EUR-* -> ED50; TOY-* -> Tokyo; OGB-* -> OSGB36; and so on. Keep the table in one shared JSON fixture for both platforms. Honour /Units (FT or US survey feet). When a declared LGIDict can't be decoded, show a message instead of silently using the camera fallback.
findings.proving_test: Fixture 1: LGIDict /Description (Layers) with a CTM mapping Neatline 0..600 x 0..400 to 550000..556000 E and 4180000..4184000 N, /Projection << /ProjectionType (UT) /Zone 10 /Hemisphere (N) /Datum (NAR-C) >>. Assert that bounds equal the inverse UTM of those corners (about 37.76-37.80N, -122.43 to -122.36). Today both return nil or fallback. Fixture 2: the forum's LE/NAS-E dictionary with a matching CTM, asserting non-nil bounds on both platforms.

findings.title: LGIDict entry selection differs between platforms: iOS reads only /CTM on 'Layers' or entries[0]; Android prefers /Registration and takes the first entry that decodes; neither ranks entries by neatline size
findings.description: iOS never reads /Registration (grep finds no references on iOS). It chooses the entry whose Description string equals 'Layers', matched through dictString only, so a Name /Layers does not match. Otherwise it takes entries[0], and if that entry fails it goes to the known-sheet table or the camera fallback. Android matches 'Layers' as either a Name or a String, uses Registration before CTM, and loops over the candidates returning the first that decodes. The Adobe path uses largest-area selection with a fail-closed rule, but neither LGIDict path does anything similar.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) An LGIDict with /Registration but no /CTM (the spec allows either). Android georeferences it; iOS returns crop-only and places it at the camera, or at the hard-coded approximate Holsworthy bounds. The same sheet ends up in different places on the two phones. (b) A multi-frame TerraGo PDF with entries [(Location Map) inset, (Main Map)] and no 'Layers'. Both platforms place the whole page using the inset's CTM, a kilometre-scale error. If the inset's datum is unsupported, iOS gives up while Android moves on to the main map, so they disagree again.
findings.suggested_fix: On both platforms: collect every entry that decodes (from Registration or CTM), rank them by neatline area, and fail closed if a larger declared entry is malformed, as the Adobe path does. Add Registration parsing on iOS with Android's precedence. Match Description as either a Name or a String.
findings.proving_test: Fixture: LGIDict array with no Description. Entry 0 is an inset: Neatline 500..550 x 300..350, CTM mapping to a 1 deg box. Entry 1 is the main map: Neatline 0..600 x 0..400, CTM to a 0.1 deg box. Assert that both platforms return the main-map bounds; today both return the inset's. Second fixture: Registration-only, with 4 points [x y lon lat] and ProjectionType LL. Assert equal non-nil bounds on iOS and Android; today iOS returns nil.

findings.title: Neatline and collar cropping is inconsistent: iOS baked tiles show collar strips the live overlay hides, and Android never crops (legend and white margins cover the basemap)
findings.description: For LGIDict sheets, the iOS live overlay is cropped to the neatline bbox (pdfRenderRect). PDFTiler, however, draws the whole MediaBox and clips only to each strip, over a coverage of neatline bounds x 1.2. Baked offline tiles therefore include a band of legend and title marginalia that is cut along arbitrary lat/lon tile edges. Android keeps no crop at all. The live bitmap is the whole CropBox, and coverage and tiles span the full page. As a result, collar, legend and white paper margins sit on top of the basemap. This differs from iOS on LGIDict sheets, although for SF North the Adobe BBox is almost the whole page on both.
findings.failure_scenario: On iOS, 'save offline' on an ADF LGIDict sheet: the cleanly cropped live map is replaced by tiles with ragged strips of legend text around the neatline. On Android the same sheet shows its title block and a white margin covering neighbouring terrain at every zoom level.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the crop (the neatline polygon, or the BBox) through PdfMapSource on both platforms. Clip the live overlay and the tile render to it: ctx.clip to the transformed pdfRenderRect in PDFTiler.renderTile, and add a crop plus a clip path in the Android PdfGroundLayer/PdfTiler. Derive coverage from the crop corners.
findings.proving_test: iOS: LGIDict fixture with a solid black collar outside a white neatline area. Run PDFTiler.generate and assert that no tile pixel whose lat/lon lies outside the neatline is black. Android: assert that the PdfGroundLayer corners and the PdfTiler coverage equal the transformed neatline or BBox corners, not the page corners.

verdicts.reasoning:
I inflated the object streams of samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf myself. Page 20 has /Rotate 0, MediaBox and CropBox [0 0 1728 2088], and three viewports. The first is 'Map Layers': BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373], Measure 424 with LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514]. The other two are 'Quadrangle Location' (area about 5,006 pt^2) and 'Adjoining Sheet Diagram' (about 3,336 pt^2), both with LPTS inside [0,1].

iOS: GeoPDFReader.swift:349-350 `(0.0...1.0).contains(normalX/Y)` makes viewportAffine return nil for the main body. That puts its area (about 3.51M) into largestMalformedDeclaredGeoArea (:216). The check at :221-225 then rejects the whole file, :84-85 returns nil, and ContentView.swift:1962 uses fallbackBounds (a 10 km square at the camera) with fromGeoPDF=false, so kind is .calibratedPDF. handleImport sets no message. LayersSheet.swift:177-181 then labels the sheet 'Manually placed bounds', because the fallback bounds are non-nil.

Android: GeoPdfParser.kt:206 `nx !in 0.0..1.0` leads to the same largest-malformed rejection at :233-236. parse returns null, and MapScreenHelpers.kt:495 returns PdfMapSource.imported, whose fallback box (PdfMapSource.kt:58-70) is 10 km x aspect 0.828, so about 8.3 x 10 km. PdfGroundLayer draws that box (CustomMapOverlays.kt:866-872), and MapScreen.kt:463 still shows the 'Imported' toast.

GDAL's pdfdataset.cpp (fetched, around line 7276) maps LPTS linearly with no range check. I reproduced the would-be affine: page (0,0)->(37.728854,-122.520123) and (1728,2088)->(37.888180,-122.353903). Both platforms' tests assert that LPTS 1.1 is rejected (PDFImportSmokeTests.swift:195-218 and :338; PdfImportHardeningInstrumentedTest.kt:314-338). iOS PDFSessionStore.save/load (:77-112, :212-232) restores the persisted fallback bounds without re-parsing. This misregisters the repo's documented demo GeoPDF on both platforms, silently, so it is critical.

Both platforms reduce the georeference to one lat/lon affine. On iOS: GeoPDFReader.swift:359 (Adobe) and :839 (LGIDict, after inverse-projecting the neatline corners at :787-815). On Android: MapScreenHelpers.kt:497 fits it, and the overlay (PDFOverlay.swift:253-275, CustomMapOverlays.kt:858-865) and both tilers use it.

I re-ran the numbers with my own Krueger-series TM for GRS80. The sample's GPTS project to a UTM rectangle (542188/556923 E, 4176319/4193606 N). A PDF->UTM affine fits them to 0.22 m, while the lat/lon affine leaves 7.9 m at every GPTS. The printed 1 km grid intersections are off by 0.75 m minimum and 6.43 m maximum: 543000E 4177000N is 6.37 m off, and 550000E 4185000N is 3.35 m off. The quad corners are 4.73-5.03 m off.

For graticule-cornered sheets drawn in UTM, the error is 4.6 m on a 7.5' sheet, 18.4 m on a 15' sheet, 148 m on a 30'x60' sheet and 588 m on a 1x2 deg sheet. On Mercator sheets the error is 186 m (1x1 deg at 37.5N) and 1.68 km (2x2 deg at 60N), with zero corner residual, so no residual check can catch it.

The Adobe path has no RMS or crossValidated gate on either platform. The iOS LGIDict path gates at RMS <= 50 m (:839-845), so a 1:100k LGIDict sheet (RMS 148 m) falls to the camera fallback on iOS, while Android places it (no gate). samples/README.md explicitly recommends Geoscience Australia 1:100k/1:250k GeoPDFs.

GDAL (pdfdataset.cpp around 7251-7300) reprojects GPTS into the projected SRS and fits there, which confirms the correct approach. The error is small on 1:24k but large at 1:50k and smaller scales, so high is fair.

From the /GCS WKT, iOS measurePrimeMeridian (GeoPDFReader.swift:395-416) and Android primeMeridianOffset (GeoPdfParser.kt:252-262) extract only PRIMEM. GPTS lat/lon go straight into the fit as WGS84 (iOS :343-357, Android :211-216). No DATUM or SPHEROID is read anywhere on the Adobe path; DatumShift/LgiDatum are applied only in the LGIDict code. GDAL (pdfdataset.cpp:7225-7260) treats GPTS as coordinates in m_oSRS.CloneGeogCS(), the GCS's own datum, and transforms them, as ISO 32000 intends.

I recomputed the magnitudes with a 3-parameter geocentric shift: NAD27 at SF 93.0 m, NAD27 at Denver 49.0 m, ED50 at Berlin 107.2 m, Tokyo 465.3 m. The sample's NAD83 GCS is about 1 m from WGS84, so the sample is unaffected. A NAD27 or ED50 GeoPDF is plausible (USGS historical quads, European producers), and it would be silently 50-460 m off on both platforms.

I reproduced this with my own macOS PDFKit probe (swift script under scratchpad/verify/probe). With MediaBox [50 50 450 350], translate(-minX,-minY) followed by page.draw(with:.mediaBox) put the square drawn at user 100..109 at user 50..59: PDFKit subtracts the box origin a second time. cg.drawPDFPage put it correctly at 100..109. With /Rotate 90, draw(with:) put the square at y 290..299, rotated into the unrotated canvas and clipped; drawPDFPage put it at 100..109. A CropBox-only file rendered correctly.

PDFRasteriser.render (PDFOverlay.swift:132-138) and PDFTiler.renderTile (PDFTiler.swift:207-210) both use exactly this transform plus draw(with:.mediaBox). No rotation or /Rotate handling exists anywhere under ios/TacticalMaps/Calibration or in ContentView (grep), and PDFMapImporter.copyAndValidate does not check it. Android rejects any rotation != 0 (MapScreenHelpers.kt:433-437, GeoPdfParser.kt:101-111), so the platforms diverge.

One extra consequence: a plain landscape PDF with /Rotate 90, which scanners often produce, also comes out clipped with a blank strip on iOS before the user even calibrates. This rests on macOS PDFKit behaviour; an XCTest on the simulator running the proposed pixel check would confirm the iOS runtime, which shares the implementation.

PdfPageInfo stores ints (PdfPageRenderer.kt:19-24) taken from PdfRenderer.Page.getWidth/getHeight, which AOSP fills with SetIntField from FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndex doubles, truncating them.

GeoPdfParser produces correspondences in raw PDFBox user space: BBox at :211-212, and Neatline/MediaBox at :359-369. PdfGroundLayer maps the full-page bitmap corners to raw (0,0)-(w_int,h_int) (CustomMapOverlays.kt:858-865). PdfTiler.pageRectForBand assumes device=(x, h_int-y) with origin 0 (PdfTiler.kt:202-209), and calibratedPdfBounds uses the same corners (PdfMapSource.kt:80-92).

pdfium renders relative to CropBox∩MediaBox with a y-flip. The null-transform path used by renderFirstPage goes through GetDisplayMatrix, which subtracts the box origin on every Android version. The matrix path used by the tiler (modern FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix) builds FX_RECT from int page sizes, so the result is a Wi/W and Hi/H scale.

Worked through: with CropBox [36 36 ...] every feature shifts 36 pt. For A-series pages the error grows from 0 at the bottom/left to frac(H) or frac(W) at the top/right. A4's 841.89 gives about 0.89 pt, which is 8 m at 1:25k and 16 m at 1:50k. iOS draws the MediaBox with doubles, so it is unaffected by CropBox. I cannot run pdfium here. The proposed androidTest pixel check would settle whether a given Android version shifts or scales, but the error exists in the live-overlay path on every version.

I checked GDAL's real LGIDict parser (pdfdataset.cpp, fetched). ProjectionType codes are 'GEOGRAPHIC' (6461), 'UT', and 'LE' for Lambert Conformal Conic (6588); there is no 'LC' and no 'LL'. Datum strings follow OGC Annex A: 'WE'/'WGE' (6252), 'NAR'/'NAR-*' (6257), 'NAS'/'NAS-*' (6262), 'GDS' for GDA94 (6278), 'OHA-*' and others.

iOS knownDatumCodes (GeoPDFReader.swift:487-489) and parseDatum (:545-547) accept only the 2-letter set, and the projection switch (:706-778) has only LL/LONGLAT/UT/UTM/TC/LC. Android LgiDatum.fromCode (LgiProjection.kt:72-83) and projectionConverter (GeoPdfParser.kt:401-441) behave the same way.

Outcomes:
- 'GEOGRAPHIC' is not LL, so it is treated as projected, requires an explicit datum, then hits the switch default and returns nil.
- 'LE' goes to the default case.
- 'WGE', 'NAR-C' and 'GDS' fail parseDatum.

iOS then returns crop-only (:672-675 / :781-784) and falls to the known-sheet table or the camera fallback. Android's converter is null, and it uses the base camera box with the 'Imported' toast. Both are silent and both behave the same. Projected LGIDict-only files (legacy TerraGo, NGA) are plausible for a tactical user, so high.

iOS selects `entries.first { dictString(dict, "Description") == "Layers" } ?? entries[0]` (GeoPDFReader.swift:589-591). dictString uses only CGPDFDictionaryGetString (:451-455), so a Name /Layers does not match. iOS reads only /CTM (:597-604), and grep finds no 'Registration' anywhere in ios/TacticalMaps.

Android matches Layers as a Name or a String (GeoPdfParser.kt:287, :487-493), prefers Registration over CTM (:295-310), and loops until an entry decodes (:289-316).

So a Registration-only LGIDict gets georeferenced on Android, while iOS returns crop-only, which leads to the camera fallback or the approximate knownSheets bounds. Neither platform ranks entries by neatline area. GDAL does (pdfdataset.cpp:5985-6034 picks the largest neatline unless Description matches), and GDAL prefers CTM over Registration, the opposite of Android. The divergence is real but needs specific LGIDict layouts, so medium is appropriate.

On iOS the live overlay rasterises only pdfRenderRect = bounds.pdfCropRect: the neatline bbox for LGIDict, or the BBox for Adobe (PDFMapSource.swift:67 and :96-97; PDFOverlay.swift:108-137). PDFTiler.renderTile, however, draws the whole MediaBox and clips only to the tile band (PDFTiler.swift:201-210) over coverage = bounds span x 1.2 (PDFMapSource.swift:57-62). Baked tiles therefore show collar and legend in a roughly 10% margin band, ending at arbitrary tile edges. This also applies to Adobe sheets whose BBox is smaller than the page, not only LGIDict sheets.

Android carries no crop at all. renderFirstPage renders the full CropBox, PdfGroundLayer maps full-page corners (CustomMapOverlays.kt:858-865), coverage comes from page corners (PdfMapSource.kt:87-92), and the tiler gates on the whole page (PdfTiler.kt:211-215).

Registration is still correct; this is a visible aesthetic and platform-consistency problem on every collared sheet. The user explicitly listed aesthetics, so I rate it medium rather than low.

verify.missed:
Missed defect (both platforms, high): the on-device tilers ignore the rotation and shear of the calibration affine when rendering. iOS PDFTiler.stripRect (ios/TacticalMaps/Calibration/PDFTiler.swift:155-170) and renderTile (:204-210) inverse-map each strip's 4 lat/lon corners, take their axis-aligned bounding CGRect, and draw it with a pure scale and translate (`scaleBy(size/r.width, -bandH/r.height)`, `translateBy(-r.minX,-r.maxY)`). Android PdfTiler.pageRectForBand (android/app/src/main/java/com/tacmap/calibration/PdfTiler.kt:193-218) does the same, feeding a bounding RectF to setRectToRect(FILL) (PdfPageRenderer.kt:183-184). Any rotation between the page axes and north is therefore dropped inside every tile, and the content is also shrunk by the bbox growth. The live overlays handle rotation correctly: iOS via the parallelogram at PDFOverlay.swift:253-275, Android via setPolyToPoly at CustomMapOverlays.kt:875-880. So baked MBTiles disagree with the live view, and lines break at every tile seam.

I simulated it in scratchpad/verify/d1skeptic/tilerot.py. The maximum error within a 256 px tile is 1.5 px at 0.34 deg (the SF North grid convergence), 4.4 px at 1 deg, 12.8 px at 3 deg and 20.6 px at 5 deg. 3-5 deg is typical for a hand-scanned or photographed paper map calibrated with fiduciaries, and also for UTM sheets near a zone edge at high latitude.

Proving test: calibrate a synthetic PDF, containing a straight black line across the page, with an affine rotated 3 deg. Run PDFTiler.generate and PdfTiler.generate, decode two horizontally adjacent tiles at maxZoom, and assert the line's row matches within 1 px at their shared edge. Today it jumps about 10+ px.

Minor related divergence: GDAL prefers /CTM over /Registration (pdfdataset.cpp around 6090-6167), while Android prefers Registration (GeoPdfParser.kt:295-310). The same file can decode differently from the reference implementation when both are present and disagree.

audit.summary:
How it works end to end.

iOS: Layers → "Calibrate with fiduciaries…" calls ContentView.startCalibration, which calls CalibrationSession.start. That seeds any manual fiduciaries already on the source. Each tap goes through MapEditingController.onTap to PDFImageOverlayView.pdfPoint(forScreenTap:). That function inverts the overlay's real UIView transform, so the PDF point is exact at any zoom, heading, rotation or shear. CalibrationInputSheet takes a full MGRS string. The NGA parser turns it into the SW corner of the cell, and GDA94 is shifted to WGS84 if chosen. The result is stored as Fiduciary(pdfX, pdfY, lat, lon). Finish needs 3 or more points and calls AffineFitter.fit. That is a least-squares fit using normal equations and Cramer's rule, taking PDF user-space points to WGS84 lon/lat. The collinearity check uses the covariance eigenvalue ratio. A new PDFMapSource then gets the calibration. The page is drawn as a parallelogram from the affine-projected corners, and PDFSessionStore saves it both as the active map and in a library keyed by content hash. Restore and re-import work.

Android: Layers → "Calibrate PDF Map" puts plain `remember` state in MapScreen. Taps go MapInputOverlay (tap-only) → camera.fromScreen → pdfPointFor, which is a linear ratio across the axis-aligned coverage box. CalibrationInputDialog uses MgrsFormatter.parse (NGA Java) plus the datum shift. Finish uses the same fitter and then PdfMapSource.calibrated. PdfGroundLayer draws the page with a 4-corner polyToPoly, and PdfSessionStore saves it.

What is solid:
- The two AffineFitter ports are line-for-line the same: same normal equations, same 1e-6 spread threshold, same equirectangular residual.
- testdata/affine_fits.json passes on both.
- I re-ran the solve in float64: realistic page coordinates recover exact transforms to under 0.1 mm.
- The Helmert constants are identical on both platforms.
- The iOS tap-to-PDF conversion and persistence are correct.
- Mixing UTM zones is harmless today, because each MGRS is converted to lat/lon on its own.

What is weak:
- The model space. Fitting straight to lon/lat misregisters UTM-gridded sheets by 16–50 m at 1:50k (45°N) and 100–170 m at 1:100k. The on-screen display on both platforms has the same error.
- Baked tiles drop any rotation in the calibration.
- On Android, calibration mode has no pan or zoom, and re-calibration ignores the existing affine.
- Only three datums are offered.
- The UX: RMS is never shown on iOS, and 3-point fits report "0m" on Android. No platform can delete or undo a point. Unreferenced PDFs are shown at a made-up location with no warning. Validation is loose.

The shared fixture only tests exactly-affine input. It cannot catch the model error or the Android tap-mapping bug.

My scripts are in scratchpad/audit/d2/: affine_model_error.py, tiler_rotation.py, android_recal.py, datum_err.py, geometry_quality.py and j/P.java.

findings.title: Android calibration mode has no pan/zoom at all; drags and pinches register as calibration taps
findings.description: While isCalibratingPdf is true, CustomMapScreen composes MapInputOverlay: a full-screen Box whose only handler is detectTapGestures. It also skips MapItemTouchOverlayCustom (the `if (!drawingInputEnabled && !calibrationInputEnabled ...)` gate at :294). That overlay is the only place pan, pinch and rotate are handled (applyCustomMapTransform at CustomMapTouch.kt:289-300). TileMapView is created with gesturesEnabled = false (:236). So the camera is frozen at wherever it was when the user tapped "Calibrate PDF Map". There are no zoom buttons in MapScreen. detectTapGestures does not cancel on movement inside bounds, so a one-finger pan attempt (or a pinch) fires onCalibrationTap at the lift-off point. That opens the fiduciary dialog for a point the user never chose. iOS keeps TileMapView pan and pinch working during calibration. Draw and measure modes share the same root cause.
findings.failure_scenario: A 1:50k sheet (20 km) is fitted to a 411-dp phone screen, about 49 m per dp. The user starts calibration. They cannot zoom in to read the grid numbers or put a finger precisely on an intersection. Finger error of about ±5 dp is about ±250 m per point, so with 3 points the map is misregistered by hundreds of metres while the toast says "Calibration RMS 0m". If they zoomed in first, the other corners of the sheet are out of reach, and Cancel throws away the points already placed. Trying to pan pops up a "Fiduciary #N" dialog.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the transform gesture path active in input modes. In MapInputOverlay (or a shared gesture node), treat a single pointer that stays within touch slop and lifts as a calibration or draw tap. Send multi-touch or beyond-slop movement to applyCustomMapTransform, the same way MapItemTouchOverlayCustom does.
findings.proving_test: androidTest with ComposeTestRule. Render CustomMapScreen(calibrationInputEnabled = true, onCameraIdle = capture, onCalibrationTap = counter). Run performTouchInput { pinch(...) } and assert the captured zoom went up. Run performTouchInput { swipeLeft() } and assert the centre moved and onCalibrationTap was not called. Both assertions fail today.

findings.title: Android re-calibration maps taps to PDF points through the axis-aligned coverage bbox, ignoring the live affine
findings.description: PdfGroundLayer draws a calibrated page (or an auto-fitted GeoPDF, which importPdfMapSource stores as Calibration.Fiduciaries) through its affine, so the page appears as a rotated or sheared quad. pdfPointFor turns the tap's lat/lng into a PDF point with a linear ratio across `coverage`. That is calibratedPdfBounds, the axis-aligned bbox of the four transformed corners. Whenever the existing transform has any rotation (a skewed scan, grid convergence, a GeoPDF), each new point is wrong by roughly sheetSize × sinθ. The seeded fiduciaries keep their correct coordinates, so the refit mixes consistent and inconsistent points. Taps are also clamped into [-5%, 105%] instead of being rejected. iOS inverts the overlay's real transform and is correct.
findings.failure_scenario: A 1134-pt (20 km) sheet was calibrated with a 2° rotation. The user reopens Calibrate to add a 4th point at a grid intersection at PDF (113.4, 113.4). It is stored as (144.0, 113.4): 30.6 pt, about 540 m, off. A 0.4° rotation, similar to the USGS sample's convergence, still gives 110–140 m. "Refining" makes the map worse, and nothing tells the user.
findings.suggested_fix: When source.calibration has a transform, compute transform.inverted().apply(lng, lat) and reject taps outside 0..pageWidth and 0..pageHeight. Only use the bbox ratio when calibration == null, which is the case where the page is drawn into that bbox.
findings.proving_test: Unit test. Build PdfMapSource.imported(...).calibrated(T, fids) where T is a 2° rotated transform (a=2.2396e-4, b=-7.821e-6, c=10, d=5.530e-6, e=1.58366e-4, f=45) on a 1134×1134 page. Take P = (113.4, 113.4), compute (lat, lng) = T.apply(P), and assert pdfPointFor(lat, lng) is within 0.5 pt of P. Today it returns (144.0, 113.4).

findings.title: Affine fitted in lon/lat cannot represent a UTM-gridded sheet: 16–50 m at 1:50k, 100–170 m at 1:100k
findings.description:
Both platforms fit lon = a·x + b·y + c and lat = d·x + e·y + f. A grid-aligned UTM sheet is linear in (E, N). In lon/lat, a rectangle of grid is a trapezoid, because the degrees of longitude per metre change with tan φ across the sheet, and a 6-parameter affine cannot represent that. The display path has the same error: iOS places a parallelogram and Android a 4-corner homography, both in Web Mercator. Fitting a homography in lon/lat, or an affine in Web Mercator, does not help (simulated 15.1 m and 15.6 m against 15.9 m). I simulated with Krüger transverse Mercator, using grid-intersection fiduciaries 10% in from each corner. Maximum misregistration inside the sheet:
- 1:25k, 10 km sheet: 4.0 m at 45°N, 6.9 m at 60°N (3 points: 12.7 m and 21.9 m).
- 1:50k, 20 km sheet: 15.9 m and 27.5 m (3 points: 50.6 m and 87.4 m).
- 1:100k, 50 km sheet: 100 m and 172 m.
- 1:250k: 640 m to 1.1 km.
The on-screen error on iOS and Android matches the fit error to within 2 m, so both platforms agree and are both wrong. The printed grid and the MGRS overlay visibly separate.
findings.failure_scenario: A 1:50k sheet at 45°N (zone 32, SW corner E490000 N4973000). The user enters 3 grid intersections exactly, at the SW, SE and NW corners. The NE grid corner is drawn 50.6 m from where it should be, and the centre is off by 11 m. At z15 on a phone, the overlay grid line sits about 15 pt from the printed line. It is worse for 60°N users and for 1:100k sheets.
findings.suggested_fix: Fit in the sheet's own grid. MGRS already gives (zone, E, N); convert any point outside the majority zone into that zone. Fit PDF → (E, N) with an affine, which is exact for grid-aligned sheets and very close for graticule-bounded TM sheets. Store the zone and hemisphere. Render through a mesh warp (Android Canvas.drawBitmapMesh; iOS subdivided quads or Metal). For tiles, invert per pixel or per block through UTM. At minimum, allow a bilinear or second-order model once there are 6 or more points.
findings.proving_test: Add a "utm_50k_45N" case to testdata/affine_fits.json. Fiduciaries: the lat/lon of zone-32 intersections E492000/E508000 × N4975000/N4991000, with PDF points = (E − 490000, N − 4973000) / 50000 / 0.000352778. Hold-outs: the sheet corners and centre, with their true lat/lon. Assert the hold-out error is under 3 m on both SharedVectors tests. Today it is 15.9 m with 4 points and 50.6 m with 3.

findings.title: Offline tile baking drops the rotation/shear of the calibration (strip bbox + axis-aligned scale)
findings.description: Each tile strip is rendered from the axis-aligned bounding rect of the strip's four corners after mapping them through the inverse affine. It uses a pure scale: ctx.scaleBy/translateBy on iOS and Matrix.setRectToRect(FILL) on Android. Any rotation or shear in the fiduciary affine is thrown away for each strip. Content is shrunk by cosθ + sinθ and left unrotated, and adjacent tiles no longer agree at their edges. The live overlay is correct on both platforms, so the user sees a good calibration and then bakes a bad one for offline use.
findings.failure_scenario: A scanned sheet calibrated with a 2° skew. Every baked tile has up to 8.9 px of in-tile error: about 30 m at z15 and about 240 m at z12. Grid lines jump by up to about twice that at tile seams. A 5° skew gives 22 px. Even the 0.37° convergence of a typical GeoPDF gives about 1.8 px of staircase.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each strip the full affine. Map the tile-pixel corners (0, top), (256, top) and (0, bottom) through the inverse affine to PDF space, and build the matrix from those 3–4 point pairs: CGAffineTransform concatenation on iOS, Matrix.setPolyToPoly on Android. Do not use a bounding rect.
findings.proving_test: Pure-math unit test on both platforms. Use a transform with a 2° rotation and one z15 tile over the page. Map tile pixels (0,0), (256,0), (0,256), (256,256) and (128,128) through the strip matrix the tiler builds, and compare with inverse.apply(tile lon/lat). Assert the difference is under 0.5 px. Today it is about 8.9 px at the corners.

findings.title: Fiduciary datum list has only WGS84/GDA94/GDA2020; legacy-datum sheets land 170–800 m off while the grid overlay looks perfect
findings.description:
Typed MGRS is always parsed on the WGS84 ellipsoid. The only other datum choices are GDA94 and GDA2020, which differ by about 2 m. The GeoPDF path already carries ED50, NAD27, Tokyo, SK-42, OSGB, NTF and CH1903 shifts (DatumShift and LgiDatum), but manual calibration cannot use them. Because the printed grid numbers are treated as WGS84, the app's MGRS grid lines up exactly with the printed grid. That hides the error, while GPS, sync and waypoint positions are displaced. I computed the offset when a legacy sheet's printed UTM is treated as WGS84:
- ED50, Germany: 218 m
- ED50, Spain: 230 m
- NAD27, California: 215 m
- NAD27, Virginia: 213 m
- SK-42: 166 m
- Tokyo: 815 m
findings.failure_scenario: A user calibrates an ED50 1:50k military sheet, or an older NAD27 USGS quad, with 4 grid intersections. The MGRS overlay matches the printed grid, so everyone trusts it. The user's GPS dot and friendly-unit markers plot about 220 m from their true positions on the sheet.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the legacy datums to the Datum enum on both platforms, reusing the GeoPDF parameters. Parse MGRS to (zone, E, N), inverse-project on that datum's ellipsoid, then apply the Helmert shift to WGS84. Persist the datum per PDF, and prompt for it at the start of calibration (sheet legends state the datum).
findings.proving_test: Unit test: with an ED50 option, the printed ED50 intersection 32U E500000 N5540000 (32UNA 00000 40000) should be stored within 5 m of its WGS84 truth (inverse TM on International 1924, then −87, −98, −121). Today there is no ED50 option, and parsing as WGS84 is about 218 m off.

findings.title: Non-georeferenced PDFs are silently placed as a 10 km box at the camera and presented as a usable map (iOS even labels them calibrated)
findings.description: A plain PDF gets fallback bounds of 10 km around the camera and becomes the active map. The MGRS grid, crosshair MGRS readout, GPS dot, measure tool and waypoint placement all work on it as if it were georeferenced. The only feedback is an "Imported <name>" toast on Android and nothing on iOS. On iOS, the source kind is .calibratedPDF (fromGeoPDF false), and because bounds are not nil the Layers sheet says "Manually placed bounds". The "No georeferencing — using map-centre fallback" string at LayersSheet.swift:178 can never appear after an import. Calibration is only reachable from Layers → Imported Map.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports a scanned 1:50k while standing in the area. The sheet appears centred on their position at a believable scale. They read a grid off the crosshair or drop a waypoint on a feature. Those coordinates are made up and can be kilometres off, with no indication.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist an explicit fallback or unreferenced placement state. Show a persistent "Not georeferenced — Calibrate" banner. Offer to start calibration right after import. Hide or grey out the MGRS readout and grid over an unreferenced sheet.
findings.proving_test: UI test on each platform. Import a PDF with no /VP or LGIDict and assert that a not-georeferenced banner or calibration prompt appears. On iOS, also assert that source.kind is not .calibratedPDF and that the Layers row shows "No georeferencing…". Both fail today.

findings.title: Fit quality is never shown usefully: iOS RMS is cleared before display, Android toasts "RMS 0m" for 3-point fits, no per-point residuals
findings.description: iOS: finish() sets lastFitRMSMetres, but finishCalibration then calls calibration.cancel() (:1936). That clears the RMS and hides the overlay, and start() also clears it. So "Previous fit RMS" only appears when selectMapSource fails. Android shows one short toast, "Calibration RMS %d m", after the calibration is already applied. Neither platform uses crossValidated. A 3-point fit, the minimum the UI asks for, always passes exactly through its points, so RMS is 0 and Android shows "0m". Neither platform computes or shows per-point residuals, so a mistyped point cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Point 3 of 3 is typed as 56HLH 34900 53288 instead of 52288, a 1 km digit slip. The sheet is sheared by about 1 km. Android says "Calibration RMS 0m" and iOS says nothing. With 4 points, one bad point pushes residuals into the hundreds of metres. iOS still shows nothing, and Android shows a single number with no way to tell which point is at fault.
findings.proving_test: iOS: an XCUITest or view-model test places 4 fiduciaries, one with a 1 km error, taps Finish, and asserts a residual summary appears with that point flagged. Android: a Compose test asserts that a 3-point fit shows "unverified" rather than "Calibration RMS 0m". Both fail today.

findings.title: No way to delete, move, edit or undo a fiduciary; Cancel wipes everything unconfirmed; in-progress calibration is not persisted
findings.description: CalibrationSession.removeFiduciary exists on iOS but nothing calls it. Android has no remove at all. Neither platform supports undo, dragging a placed marker, or editing a point's MGRS. The small Cancel button sits right next to Finish and discards every point immediately with no confirmation. The draft lives only in memory: an iOS @StateObject and Android remember{} (not rememberSaveable). It is lost if the OS kills the app while the user switches away to look up a grid or photograph the paper map. On Android it is also lost on any configuration change not listed in configChanges, such as a uiMode change.
findings.failure_scenario: Five points have been placed carefully and point 4 has a typo. The only options are to accept a bad fit or to Cancel and redo all five, reading every grid label again. One stray tap on Cancel loses all of them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fiduciary list where tapping a marker lets you edit its MGRS, move it or delete it. Add an undo for the last point and a confirmation on Cancel when at least one point exists. Persist the draft (points plus datum) keyed by the PDF content hash, and restore it when calibration reopens.
findings.proving_test: UI test: place 3 points, delete #2 from the list, and assert there are 2 points and the marker is gone. Background-kill and relaunch the app, and assert the draft is back. There is no delete control today, and the draft is lost.

findings.title: iOS Finish silently does nothing when the fit fails; corner-bounds failure yields a misleading 'Map change not saved' + 'add more fiduciaries' hint
findings.description: When AffineFitter.fit throws (degenerate, invalidInput or invalidResult), finish() only print()s and returns nil, and finishCalibration returns. Finish stays enabled because canFinish only counts to 3, so the button does nothing and nothing is shown. Android at least shows a toast. A second case: the fit succeeds but applyCalibration rejects the page-corner bounds, for example when a zone typo ("5…" for "56…") spreads the points 150° apart and the corners go past ±180°. Then newSource keeps bounds nil, PDFSessionStore.save returns false, and the user gets the generic "Map change not saved" alert. The overlay then shows "Previous fit RMS… add more fiduciaries", which is wrong advice. In the same case, Android's calibrated() returns `this`, and MapScreen still toasts success.
findings.failure_scenario: The user carefully places 3 grid ticks along the bottom margin at high zoom, so they are collinear. Finish does nothing, no matter how often they tap it. There is no way to delete a point, so the only way out is Cancel.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn AffineFitError into a localized alert that says why and what to do (Android already has the strings). Check the page-corner bounds as part of the fit and report a failure there too. On Android, check whether calibrated() actually changed anything before announcing success.
findings.proving_test: Test: a session with 3 collinear points ((0,0), (500,0), (1000,0)). Call finishCalibration and assert an error message is published or presented. Today there is no state change.

findings.title: Near-collinear or clustered control points are accepted (1e-6 spread threshold); extrapolation errors of hundreds of metres to km with RMS 0
findings.description:
The only geometry check rejects a point set when the ratio of the minor to major covariance eigenvalue is below 1e-6. That means a perpendicular spread under about 0.1% of the along-line spread. Normal finger noise lifts a nearly straight set of points above that threshold, and clustered points pass easily. Nothing warns about poor spread, and the status line only says "need 3+". Monte Carlo on a 1:50k sheet (2 pt tap σ, 5 m reading σ), median worst-corner error:
- 4 points near the corners: 67 m
- 3 points along a road (spread ratio 1.2e-3): 991 m (95th percentile 2.1 km)
- 3 points in the central 15% of the sheet: 389 m
All of these are accepted, and 3-point sets report RMS 0.
findings.failure_scenario: The user picks three grid-tick labels along the bottom collar, at (100,50), (550,53) and (1000,49); the ratio is about 1e-5. The fit is accepted, and the north half of the sheet is placed kilometres off.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a real spread: for example an eigenvalue ratio above about 0.05 and a convex hull covering at least 20–25% of the page. Show a hint such as "add a point near the top-right". Only call a fit verified with 4 or more well-spread points.
findings.proving_test: Add to both AffineFitter test suites: fit([(100,50), (550,53), (1000,49)] with any consistent lat/lon) should throw degenerate or poorGeometry. Today it succeeds on both platforms.

findings.title: Fiduciary MGRS validation: 100 km/10 km refs accepted, truncated 6/8-figure refs used as SW corner, Android accepts invalid 100 km column letters
findings.description:
There are three problems.
1. Both platforms accept a bare 100 km square ("56HLH") or a 2-figure reference as a fiduciary. NGA returns the SW corner; I checked with mgrs-2.1.3: "56HLH" gives −34.322, 150.826 and "56HLH34" gives −33.967, 151.160.
2. Calibration uses the SW corner of the cell for truncated 6- and 8-figure references, while Search and waypoint entry use the cell centre (resolveGridReference). If the user taps a feature and types its standard truncated 6-figure reference, each point is biased by up to 141 m (about 71 m on average) towards the SW. All points bias the same way, so the whole sheet shifts. The UI never tells the user to tap grid intersections when using low-precision references.
3. Android does not check the zone's 100 km column letters. "56HAH3490052288" parses to −33.767, 147.980, about 300 km west (it re-encodes as 55HEC…). iOS's isSafeUTMMGRS rejects it.
findings.failure_scenario: Three fiduciaries on a church, a trig point and a bridge, entered as 6-figure references, shift the map about 50–100 m. On Android, a one-letter slip in the square ID creates a point hundreds of kilometres away, and with 3 points it still reports RMS 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Require at least 4 figures, and 8–10 for points that are not grid intersections. Show the precision the entry resolves to. Ask whether the point is a grid intersection, and use the cell centre if it is not. Port iOS's column-set check to Android.
findings.proving_test: Add "56HAH3490052288" and "56HLH" to the invalid list in testdata/mgrs_samples.json, or add a calibration-specific list. Android sharedMgrsVectors fails today on the first. A unit test that confirmFiduciary("56HLH") returns false fails on iOS today.

findings.title: Calibration input accepts only a full MGRS string: no lat/lon (DD/DMS), UTM or local shorthand; Android lacks 'use my location'
findings.description: Many topo sheets and charts, including USGS quads, print lat/lon only at the neatline corners and edges, and those are the easiest fiduciaries to use. Calibration cannot take decimal or DMS lat/lon, UTM E/N, or local shorthand like "349 522". Search and waypoint entry already handle decimal lat/lon and shorthand (SearchSheet.decimalCoordinate, resolveGridReference). Android also lacks iOS's "Use my current location" button. Users have to convert coordinates by hand, which adds a source of error.
findings.failure_scenario: Calibrating a civil topo sheet that only shows lat/lon ticks: the user must work out the MGRS of each corner elsewhere, and any conversion slip becomes a bad fiduciary. On Android, standing at a feature, there is no way to use GPS.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the Search coordinate parser, add DMS and UTM parsing, and use the first point's GZD and 100 km square as the anchor for shorthand. Add the GPS button on Android.
findings.proving_test: confirmFiduciary("37°52'30\"N 122°30'00\"W") and confirmFiduciary("-33.8568, 151.2153") should both succeed with the expected coordinates. Both return false today on both platforms.

findings.title: Placement feedback: Android pins sit at the typed geo position (not the tapped feature) with no pending marker; iOS entry sheet hides the map
findings.description: Android draws each numbered pin at the fiduciary's typed latitude and longitude (CustomMapOverlays.kt:415), not at the PDF point that was tapped. On a first calibration the page sits at its camera-centred fallback, so pins land wherever the MGRS points, often off-screen. With D2-01, the user cannot pan to them. There is also no pending marker. iOS draws markers on the page at the PDF point and shows a pending crosshair, which is good. But its MGRS entry is a full-height sheet covering the map, so the user cannot read the printed grid numbers next to the point they just tapped; the sheet shows only raw PDF coordinates. Neither platform lets the user nudge a pending point; they have to cancel and tap again.
findings.failure_scenario: Android: after 2 points the user cannot see which intersections they used and picks the same one again. iOS: the user taps an intersection, the sheet covers its labels, and they must cancel, read the labels, and tap again.
findings.suggested_fix: Android: draw pins at the PDF point through the current placement, and after fitting optionally draw a residual line to the typed position. iOS: present the input with small or medium detents and background interaction so the tapped area stays visible, add a magnified inset, and allow dragging the pending marker.
findings.proving_test: Compose screenshot test: on an uncalibrated PDF at the fallback placement, add a fiduciary at PDF (100,100) with an MGRS 50 km away. Assert the pin is drawn at the screen position of page point (100,100). Today it is drawn at the MGRS location. iOS: an XCUITest asserts that the area around the pending marker stays visible while the input is presented.

findings.title: Calibration happens on a single ≤72 dpi preview raster that is only magnified on zoom
findings.description: The bitmap users tap on while calibrating is rendered once. Its scale is min(1, 4096 / maxDim, memory limit), so it never exceeds 1 px per PDF point (72 dpi). Zooming in only magnifies it. At 1:50k, 1 pt is 17.6 m, and 6–7 pt grid numbers become 6–7 px blurs. Scanned PDFs with a 200–300 dpi embedded image lose 3–4 times their resolution. Reading labels and hitting intersections gets harder exactly when the user zooms in to be precise. Baked tiles are sharp, but baking needs a finished calibration first.
findings.failure_scenario: An A1 1:50k scan (2384×1684 pt, 300 dpi image) previews at 2384×1684 px. Zoomed in on a 3x phone, the grid label "34" is too blurry, the user reads it as "84", and the fiduciary is 5 km off.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise the preview towards the 4096 px budget even for pages under 4096 pt; today the scale is capped at 1. During calibration, re-render a sharp crop of the visible area once zooming settles (PDFKit or PdfRenderer with a region matrix).
findings.proving_test: Unit test: boundedPDFRasterSize(width: 2384, height: 1684) and boundedPdfRenderSize(2384, 1684) should give a long edge of at least 4096 px, or at least 1.7 px per pt. Today both give 2384 (scale 1.0).

findings.title: iOS fallback placement is a 10×10 km square regardless of page aspect (Android preserves aspect)
findings.description: GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds always returns a square, so an unreferenced landscape page is squashed horizontally on screen while the user calibrates it. Grid squares look 1.41 times taller than wide, and text and symbols are distorted. Android scales the width by the page aspect. Tap-to-PDF mapping uses fractions of the image, so accuracy is not affected. It is a visible difference between the platforms and makes features harder to recognise.
findings.failure_scenario: Importing a 2384×1684 pt sheet on iOS draws it 10 km × 10 km, so the printed 1 km squares appear as 1 : 1.41 rectangles during calibration.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the media box aspect into fallbackBounds (east-west half-width = 5 km × width/height), matching Android.
findings.proving_test: After adding a page-size parameter: fallbackBounds(centeredOn: c, pageSize: 2384×1684) should give an east-west to north-south span ratio of about 1.416 in metres. Today it is 1.0.

verdicts.reasoning: CustomMapScreen.kt:229-236 creates TileMapView with gesturesEnabled=false, so its detectTransformGestures block (TileMapView.kt:128) never installs. MapItemTouchOverlayCustom is the only other transform path (applyCustomMapTransform, CustomMapTouch.kt:289-300). It is skipped by the gate at CustomMapScreen.kt:294 and also returns early at CustomMapTouch.kt:131 when calibrationInputEnabled is set. While calibrating, the only pointer handler is MapInputOverlay's detectTapGestures (CustomMapTouch.kt:616-621). In Compose, waitForUpOrCancellation cancels only when the pointer is consumed or leaves bounds, and this box is full-screen. So a one-finger drag fires onCalibrationTap at the lift-off point, and a pinch fires it at the last pointer's up. The CalibrationBar (MapScreen.kt:1404) has no zoom controls. The camera is frozen at whatever zoom was set before 'Calibrate PDF Map'. Also, MapViewModel.frameCameraFor flies to z15 on the user's position after import, so a 10 km fallback page is about 7x wider than the screen at that point. iOS keeps its UIPan/UIPinch recognisers during calibration (TileMapView.swift:130-134). Drawing and measure modes share this root cause. Critical is justified: Android calibration can only be done at one coarse zoom (about 50-100 m per dp for a fitted 1:50k sheet), which gives hundreds of metres of misregistration in normal use.

MapScreen.kt:926-933 sends taps to pdfSource.pdfPointFor (MapScreenHelpers.kt:65-80). That function applies a linear lat/lon ratio across `coverage`. For a calibrated source, coverage is calibratedPdfBounds (PdfMapSource.kt:76-105), the axis-aligned bbox of the four affine corners. PdfGroundLayer, however, draws the page through the affine as a rotated quad (CustomMapOverlays.kt:852-873). startPdfCalibration (MapScreen.kt:838-848) reseeds the existing Fiduciaries calibration, and importPdfMapSource stores GeoPDFs as Fiduciaries too (MapScreenHelpers.kt:496-499). So every re-calibration uses the wrong mapping. I re-ran the auditor's transform (verify/d2/d202.py): P=(113.4,113.4) maps back to (144.01,113.4), which is 30.6 pt or 540 m off, with a worst case of 675 m over the page. A pure 0.4° rotation on a 20 km sheet gives up to 139 m. Rotations of 1-2° are normal for TM sheets away from the central meridian, because grid convergence is about Δλ·sinφ. A first calibration is correct, because the page is drawn into the same bbox. iOS uses UIView.convert through the real transform (PDFOverlay.swift:288-299).

Both fitters solve lon=a·x+b·y+c and lat=d·x+e·y+f (AffineTransform2D.swift:5-23 and :111-114; AffineTransform2D.kt:12-28 and :111-113). The file's own comment at :10-13 admits it is only good enough for prototype scales. A TM-gridded page is linear in (E,N), not in lon/lat. I simulated it independently with my own Krüger TM (verify/d2/tm.py, d203.py): zone 32, fiduciaries 10% in from the corners, worst error over the sheet. Results: 4.0/12.7 m for a 10 km sheet at 45°N (4 points/3 points), 16.0/50.9 m for 20 km, 100.6 m for 50 km, and 6.9/27.7/174.6 m for 10/20/50 km at 60°N. These match the auditor to within 1 m. testdata/affine_fits.json only has exactly-affine cases, so it cannot catch this. The display paths also build the quad from the same affine, so they cannot compensate. High is fair given the explicit requirement that the MGRS grid line up with the printed grid. At 1:50k the offset is about 5 pt at z15.

iOS stripRect (PDFTiler.swift:155-170) takes min/max of the four inverse-mapped corners. renderTile (:201-210) then applies only translate and scale (ctx.scaleBy(size/r.width, -bandH/r.height)). Android pageRectForBand (PdfTiler.kt:187-219) likewise returns an axis-aligned RectF, and PdfPageRenderer.kt:183-185 uses setRectToRect(FILL). On both platforms any rotation or shear in the affine is discarded, and the content is shrunk into the bbox. My own check (verify/d2/d204.py) gives worst in-tile errors of 1.65 px at 0.37°, 8.93 px at 2° and 22.3 px at 5°, matching the auditor. Adjacent tiles have overlapping bboxes, so content is discontinuous at seams. The live overlays are correct (iOS applyAffinePlacement; Android polyToPoly), so what the user sees before baking differs from the offline MBTiles. Rotation of 1-2° is typical for any TM sheet a few degrees off its central meridian, and for a GeoPDF whose lon/lat affine carries convergence.

The Datum enum has only wgs84/gda94/gda2020 on both platforms (Datum.swift:9-31; Datum.kt:15-25). MGRS is always decoded on WGS84 by NGA, and then toWGS84 is applied (CalibrationSession.swift:67-72; MapScreen.kt:2143-2150). I recomputed the offsets with inverse TM on the legacy ellipsoid plus the standard 3-parameter shifts (verify/d2/d205.py): ED50 Germany 218 m, ED50 Spain 230 m, NAD27 CA 215 m, NAD27 VA 213 m, Tokyo 818 m, SK-42 155 m. These agree with the auditor, apart from SK-42 at 155 m versus 166 m. Because the printed grid is treated as WGS84, the MGRS overlay lines up with it perfectly while GPS and markers are about 200 m off, so nothing warns the user. The comments show the app targets Australian MGA users, and older AMG sheets (AGD66/AGD84, about 200 m from GDA) are also missing. That makes this a plausible field case rather than an exotic one. It is a scope gap rather than a logic bug, but the result is a silent wrong position, so I keep it at high.

iOS handleImport (ContentView.swift:1961-1968) always supplies bounds (parsedBounds ?? GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds), and PDFMapSource.init sets kind=.calibratedPDF when fromGeoPDF is false (PDFMapSource.swift:56). LayersSheet.swift:176-181 checks bounds == nil, so the 'No georeferencing' string is unreachable after import, and a camera-centred placeholder is labelled 'Manually placed bounds'. Android: PdfMapSource.imported gives fallbackBounds with calibration=null (PdfMapSource.kt:43-71). The only feedback is the 'Imported %s' toast (MapScreen.kt:461-465). Neither platform prompts for calibration, shows a banner, or suppresses the MGRS readout or grid. This is the default outcome of every mode (b) import, so high is reasonable.

iOS: finish() sets lastFitRMSMetres (CalibrationSession.swift:98). finishCalibration then calls calibration.cancel() after a successful selectMapSource (ContentView.swift:1935-1936), which nils it (:52). So CalibrationOverlay.swift:40-45 only shows RMS when the switch fails. Android toasts 'Calibration RMS %d m' after applying (MapScreen.kt:861), and that reads 0 for any 3-point fit. crossValidated is never read by the UI (grep: only the definitions and the GeoPDFReader internal use). There are no per-point residuals anywhere. The facts are all correct. I downgraded to medium because this is a missing feedback surface, not a wrong result. A grossly bad point usually shows up visually as a sheared page and a misaligned printed-versus-overlay grid, even though the user cannot tell which point caused it.

CalibrationSession.removeFiduciary (CalibrationSession.swift:86-88) has no callers (grep). Android has no remove path: calibrationFiduciaries is only appended to (MapScreen.kt:2150) or reset. CalibrationOverlay Cancel (CalibrationOverlay.swift:23) and Android CalibrationBar Cancel (MapScreenChrome.kt:469) call cancel() directly with no confirmation, and that clears every point. The state lives in an iOS @StateObject (ContentView.swift:485) and in Android plain remember (MapScreen.kt:401-405). configChanges covers only orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden (AndroidManifest.xml:52), so a uiMode or locale change, or process death, loses the draft. All correct. I rated it medium: the cost is redoing the work, not a wrong map. D2-07 compounds it, because a bad point cannot be removed.

CalibrationSession.finish() catches AffineFitError, only print()s, and returns nil (:100-103). finishCalibration then silently returns (ContentView.swift:1920-1921), while Finish stays enabled because canFinish is only count>=3. In the second case, applyCalibration returns early when the corners are invalid or when minLat>=maxLat (PDFMapSource.swift:111-138). newSource.bounds stays nil, PDFSessionStore.save returns false at :78-80, and selectMapSource fails with the generic alert. calibration.cancel() is then skipped, so the overlay shows 'Previous fit RMS … add more fiduciaries', which is misleading. On Android, calibrated() returns `this` on the same failure (PdfMapSource.kt:22-27). vm.setMapSource(this) re-activates the old source, and MapScreen.kt:858-861 exits calibration and toasts a success RMS, which also drops the new points. The exact-collinear trigger is rarer than the auditor implies, because taps are rarely exactly collinear (that case is D2-10). Coincident or very-close points and zone typos still reach it. Medium is right.

The only geometry gate is minor/major eigenvalue ratio < 1e-6 (AffineTransform2D.swift:139-155; AffineTransform2D.kt:136-155, MIN_SPREAD_RATIO=1e-6). The auditor's collar example (100,50),(550,53),(1000,49) has a ratio of 2.0e-5 and is accepted on both platforms. My own Monte Carlo on 1:50k (2 pt tap σ, 5 m reading σ; verify/d2/d210.py) gives a worst-corner median of 66 m for 4 corner points and 369 m for 3 central points, which agrees with the auditor. For the collar set I get km-scale errors (median about 13 km, even worse than the auditor's 991 m, because tap noise is comparable to the 3 pt perpendicular spread). The status lines (CalibrationOverlay.swift:53-62; MapScreenChrome.kt:488-493) never mention spread. Medium: the result is usually visibly wrong, but nothing guides the user away from it.

I ran the Android library itself (mil.nga:mgrs 2.1.3 from the gradle cache, verify/d2/j/V.java). '56HAH3490052288' parses to -33.767, 147.980 and re-encodes as 55HEC…, so it is accepted. Android parse (MgrsFormatter.kt:50-70) only regex-checks the shape. iOS isSafeUTMMGRS checks the zone%3 column set (MGRSFormatter.swift:211-226) and rejects it, so the platforms diverge. '56HLH' gives -34.322, 150.826 on Android, and iOS explicitly allows the bare prefix (:86-90). The SW-corner-versus-centre point also holds: confirmFiduciary uses MGRSFormatter.coordinate (SW corner), while resolveGridReference centres the cell (:99-105). The iOS sheet invites feature fiduciaries ('Church spire', CalibrationInputSheet.swift:29,62), so a truncated 6-figure feature ref biases the point by a mean offset of (50,50) m toward the SW. One caveat: bare 100 km or 10 km refs are legitimate when the tapped point really is that grid intersection, so sub-point 1 is only a problem for non-intersection features.

iOS confirmFiduciary accepts only MGRSFormatter.coordinate(from:) (CalibrationSession.swift:67-69; the sheet field is MGRS-only at CalibrationInputSheet.swift:45-58). Android onSave uses only MgrsFormatter.parse (MapScreen.kt:2143-2146). Decimal or DMS lat/lon, UTM E/N and shorthand are all rejected, even though Search already parses decimal coordinates and shorthand. The Android CalibrationInputDialog (MapScreenChrome.kt:495-560) has no counterpart to iOS's 'Use my current location' button (CalibrationInputSheet.swift:50-57). The feature brief itself says 'MGRS / lat-lon etc.', and many charts carry only graticule ticks, so medium is fair.

CalibrationFiduciariesLayer projects fid.latitude/longitude, the typed position (CustomMapOverlays.kt:415), not the tapped PDF point. On a first calibration the page sits at the camera-centred fallback, so pins land wherever the MGRS points, unrelated to the tapped feature. No pending marker is drawn for pendingCalibrationTap on Android. iOS draws markers at the PDF point, plus a pending crosshair (PDFOverlay.swift:312-341). But CalibrationInputSheet is presented through nightSheet, a plain .sheet with no detents (NightModeContent.swift:61-68), which is full-height on iPhone and covers the tapped area. Correct as described; it is a UX issue, so medium.

boundedPDFRasterSize (PDFOverlay.swift:69-89) and boundedPdfRenderSize (PdfPageRenderer.kt:44-60) both use scale=min(1, …), so the live raster never exceeds 1 px per PDF pt. It is rendered once (PDFRasteriser.render; PdfGroundLayer's LaunchedEffect calls renderFirstPage). Nothing re-renders at higher resolution: renderFirstPageRegion and renderFirstPageStrips are used only by PdfTiler, and there is no CATiledLayer on iOS. So calibration taps, and any zoomed viewing before baking, magnify a 72 dpi bitmap. A small nit in the proposed test: under the 32 MB cap, a 2384×1684 page can only reach about 1.44x (memoryScale), not 4096 px, unless the byte cap is also raised.

GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds (GeoPDFReader.swift:856-895) uses the same halfWidthMetres for dLat and dLon, so it always produces a 10×10 km square. ContentView.swift:1962 passes no page size. The fallback Bounds has no placementAffine, so the overlay stretches the image into the bbox and a landscape page is squashed. Android scales the width by pageInfo.aspectRatio (PdfMapSource.kt:58-71). Tap-to-PDF uses view fractions, so accuracy is unaffected. Cosmetic divergence only: low.

verify.missed: Android: calibration taps can be silently dropped, or sent to Measure, when calibration starts while another input mode is active. MapInputOverlay (android/app/src/main/java/com/tacmap/map/CustomMapTouch.kt:616-621) uses Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) { detectTapGestures { if (drawingInputEnabled) … else if (calibrationInputEnabled) … } } and reads the plain Boolean parameters inside the block, not through rememberUpdatedState. I checked the project's Compose BOM 2024.06.00 (ui 1.6.8): SuspendPointerInputElement.equals compares only the keys (I disassembled it from the gradle cache), so the running gesture coroutine keeps the booleans from when it started. (1) If a draw tool is active (overlay composed with drawingInputEnabled=true) and the user opens hamburger → Layers and Labels → Calibrate PDF Map, startPdfCalibration (MapScreen.kt:838-848) sets activeDrawTool=null and isCalibratingPdf=true in the same frame. The overlay never leaves composition, so every tap goes to handleDrawingTap, which returns because there is no tool and no measure (MapScreen.kt:798-806). Calibration taps do nothing until Cancel. (2) startPdfCalibration never stops measureSession, and drawingInputEnabled = activeDrawTool != null || measureSession.isActive (MapScreen.kt:884). Starting calibration from Measure therefore sends every tap to measure points, while the CalibrationBar branch hides the MeasureToolbar (MapScreen.kt:1404-1416). (3) In reverse, hamburger → Measure during calibration (MapScreen.kt:1203-1208) followed by Finish leaves the stale calibration=true capture active, so measure taps open the 'Fiduciary #N' dialog outside calibration. Severity: medium (reachable, because the hamburger is always visible, and the workaround is Cancel then restart calibration). Test: a Compose UI test that composes CustomMapScreen with drawingInputEnabled=true, then recomposes with drawingInputEnabled=false and calibrationInputEnabled=true, calls performClick, and asserts onCalibrationTap fired. Today onDrawingTap fires instead. Fix: key the pointerInput on (drawingInputEnabled, calibrationInputEnabled), or read them through rememberUpdatedState, and end measureSession in startPdfCalibration.

audit.summary:
How it works. Both platforms have two display paths.
