findings.failure_scenario: At z18 on a baked PDF, printed grid lines near tile edges sit half a pixel off the app grid and visibly 'breathe' by a pixel while pinching.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw tiles at exact float frames (overlap seams with a 1-pixel content bleed baked into the tiles, or disable anti-aliasing at seams) instead of inflating or rounding.
findings.proving_test: Unit test on the frame computation: for a tile at z18 and camera zoom 18.37, assert that the drawn rect equals TileMath.tileFrame exactly (iOS) and that the Android dst rect differs from f*density by under 0.01 px.

verdicts.reasoning:
I decompressed the sample's ObjStm myself. Measure 424 (the 'Map Layers' viewport, BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373]) has LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514]. The two insets (Measure 420 and 422) have LPTS [0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1] and World_Mercator GCS.

iOS: viewportAffine returns nil because of `(0.0...1.0).contains(normalX)` (GeoPDFReader.swift:349-351), so the main viewport's area goes into largestMalformedDeclaredGeoArea (line 216). bestGeo is then an inset, and the guard at lines 221-225 returns .rejected. bounds(from:) returns nil (lines 81-82), and ContentView.swift:417 then 1962 fall back to GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds around the camera.

Android: `nx !in 0.0..1.0` sets malformed (GeoPdfParser.kt:205-209). largestMalformed > bestArea gives Rejected (232-237), parse() returns null (line 78), and importPdfMapSource returns the uncalibrated `base` (MapScreenHelpers.kt:495).

The smoke test at PDFImportSmokeTests.swift:337-339 pins the strict [0,1] rule. Root cause: LPTS range validation is stricter than real USGS producers.

Both platforms fit one lat/lon-degree affine: AffineTransform2D.swift:100-134 (lon=ax+by+c, lat=dx+ey+f), and the Android equivalent. iOS places the image linearly: a basis from TL->TR and TL->BL plus the centre = mean of the 4 projected corners (PDFOverlay.swift:23-65, 253-275). Android uses a 4-corner setPolyToPoly over the whole page (CustomMapOverlays.kt:856-882).

My own Kruger-series TM script checks this:
- The sample PDF->UTM affine has a 0.22 m residual at the 4 GPTS.
- The lat/lon affine is off by up to 6.42 m at the 238 interior 1000 m intersections.
- A synthetic 15' 1:50k sheet at 48N: 21.7 m (model), 21.8 m (iOS end-to-end), 22.1 m (Android).
- At 60N: 23.9 m (model), 28.2 m (iOS), 34.3 m (Android, 100 pt collar).

These match the auditor's numbers. The LGIDict path also accepts RMS <= 50 m (GeoPDFReader.swift:838-842). Root cause: a UTM-cast sheet is affine in easting/northing, not in lat/lon, and the screen placement is linear while Mercator is not.

With 3 fiducials the lat/lon affine is exactly determined, so RMS is about 0. crossValidated is computed (AffineTransform2D.swift:133) but only read by GeoPDFReader.swift:840, never by the calibration UI.

What the user sees:
- iOS: the HUD says 'need 3+' and 'Tap Finish to apply' (CalibrationOverlay.swift:53-61), and canFinish is count>=3 (CalibrationSession.swift:90).
- Android: finishPdfCalibration toasts 'Calibration RMS %1$sm' with rmsMetres.toInt() = 0 (MapScreen.kt:850-862).

My simulation, with fiducials at 1 km intersections about 1.5 km inside the SW/NW/NE corners:
- 7.5' 1:24k: 13.2 m.
- 15' 1:50k at 48N: 77.2 m (near the CM) and 77.4 m (2.5 deg off the CM).
- 60N: 81.9 m.
- 4 points: 21.4 m.

This is a sheet misregistered by about 75+ m in a normal minimum-point calibration, while the UI reports RMS 0 m. Keeping critical.

The label comes from MGRS.from of the lat/lon-averaged segment midpoint (MGRSGridRenderer.swift:98-105; MgrsGridRenderer.kt:105-108). For a constant-northing line in the northern hemisphere, lat(lambda) is about lat0 - c*lambda^2, so the chord midpoint always lies south of the line by c*dlambda^2/4, whatever the offset from the CM.

NGA rounds UTM to cm (UTM.swift:340-347), then truncates to Int metres (MGRS.swift:412-414), so N-0.02 m becomes N-1 and the km digit drops by one. My Python emulation gives:
- Horizontal: 1 km -0.02 m ('83' for 84), 10 km -1.52 m at 38N.
- 10 km vertical west of the CM: -0.03 m, giving '4' for 5.

I then ran the real mgrs-2.1.3 jar over 37.75-37.875N, -122.5 to -122.375:
- KILOMETER: 195/390 wrong, i.e. every horizontal label (e.g. 4178000 labelled 77).
- TEN_KILOMETER: 6/6 horizontal wrong.

The southern hemisphere curvature sign reverses, so no error there.

NGA emits one segment per cell edge: GridZone.swift:151-183 appends MGRSLine(southwest, southeast) with precision spacing. Both renderers draw it as a single straight moveTo/lineTo in screen (Web Mercator) space (MGRSGridOverlayView.swift:76-87; CustomMapOverlays.kt:288-293).

My Mercator chord-to-curve script gives:
- 100 km horizontal: 153 m (38N), 216 m (48N), 344 m (60N).
- 10 km horizontal: 1.53 / 2.17 / 3.44 m.
- 1 km: 1.5-3.4 cm.
- 100 km vertical: 5-13 m at E=600000.

1 km (from z12), 10 km (from z8) and 100 km (always) are drawn together, and N=x00000 is also a 1 km line. So at z14 at 38N (7.5 m/pt) the thick 100 km chord sits about 20 pt from the correct 1 km line at mid-square. Root cause: no densification before projection.

The coverage square (TileMapContainer.swift:28-50, used at 548-566; Android orientationInvariantGridBounds, CustomMapOverlays.kt:336-353) has half-side hypot(393,852)/2 = 469 pt. It therefore reaches 43 pt above/below and 272 pt left/right of a portrait viewport.

NGA drawBounds ceils/floors to the precision (GridZone.swift:291-324), so the topmost cell on each vertical line straddles the square's top edge. Its midpoint label sits at y in [-43-L/2, -43+L/2]: always negative for L=33 pt (z12) and L=66 pt (z13).

The declutter keeps the smallest y for easting labels and the smallest x for northing labels (MGRSGridOverlayView.swift:99-113; CustomMapOverlays.kt:297-307). The kept northing label lands at x in [-272-L/2, -272+L/2], which is off-screen for every zoom up to about z16.

The crosshair readout still works, so medium is fair.

How taps are converted: onCalibrationTap calls pdfSource?.pdfPointFor(lat,lng) (MapScreen.kt:926-933). That interpolates linearly inside `coverage` (MapScreenHelpers.kt:65-80). After calibrated(), coverage is calibratedPdfBounds, the axis-aligned bbox of the 4 transformed page corners (PdfMapSource.kt:76-104).

How the page is drawn: PdfGroundLayer draws through the full affine corners (CustomMapOverlays.kt:858-865).

Why old points mix in: a GeoPDF import calls base.calibrated(), which produces Calibration.Fiduciaries (PdfMapSource.kt:22-36, MapScreenHelpers.kt:495-499). startPdfCalibration seeds those fids (MapScreen.kt:838-848), so new taps mix with exact points.

My check with a 3 deg-rotated affine on a 1400x1950 page gives up to 95 pt of tap error, about 1.7 km at 1:50k. An unrotated affine (the sample) gives about 0. iOS converts through the view's own transform (PDFOverlay.swift:288-299).

The Adobe path reads /GCS only for PRIMEM. iOS measurePrimeMeridian (GeoPDFReader.swift:395-424) feeds viewportGeoBounds and viewportAffine; Android primeMeridianOffset (GeoPdfParser.kt:252-262). GPTS are added as if WGS84, with no datum or TOWGS84 parsing.

The LGIDict path does call parseDatum or DatumShift (GeoPDFReader.swift:503-549, 672; GeoPdfParser.kt:403, 444). The manual Datum enum has only WGS84, GDA94 and GDA2020 on both platforms (Datum.swift:9-31; Datum.kt:15-24). CalibrationSession and MapScreen.kt:2144-2150 apply only that enum.

So a NAD27, ED50 or Tokyo GCS in /VP is silently treated as WGS84. For the sample (NAD83) the error is about 1 m. The bug is clear from the code; the magnitudes quoted are standard datum-shift figures.

Both tilers send the strip's lat/lon rectangle through the inverse affine and take the axis-aligned bbox:
- iOS: stripRect (PDFTiler.swift:155-170), then scaleBy(size/r.width, -bandH/r.height) and translate (191-211).
- Android: pageRectForBand (PdfTiler.kt:172-204), then setRectToRect(pageRect, dest, FILL) (PdfPageRenderer.kt:180-195).

The rotation and shear terms (b, d) are therefore thrown away. My own tile simulation at z15, where a 256 px tile maps onto the rotated PDF, gives 0 px at 0 deg, 1.6 px at 0.37 deg, 8.2 px at 1.9 deg and 12.7 px at 3 deg, which matches the auditor.

Generate Tiles then swaps the active map to the baked MBTiles (LayersSheet.swift:143-160; MapScreen.kt:2011-2030).

The Android camera viewport and zoom are in dp: MapCamera.kt uses viewportWidth in dp and TILE_SIZE 256 per 2^zoom, and TileMapView.kt:187 sets wDp. MgrsGridCanvas passes mapWidthPx = hypot(w,h)*density (CustomMapOverlays.kt:275-283) against a lon span measured in dp. The derived zoom in MgrsGridRenderer.kt:61-77 is therefore camera.zoom + log2(density), so on a 2.625 density phone the 1 km lines start at z of about 10.1. iOS passes points, which is consistent (MGRSGridRenderer.swift:58-68).

The gridBounds remember is keyed on centerLat/centerLon/zoom (lines 265-271), so build() reruns in composition on every pan frame. At z10.1 on a 411x914 dp phone the coverage square is about 113 km, i.e. about 12.8k 1 km cells and about 26k segments, and each segment also gets an MGRS.from call for its label. The 55 px bucket is confirmed too.

refreshGrid returns early unless the '%.3f' fingerprint of region centre and span changes (TileMapContainer.swift:548-566). It is called on every camera change (reprojectOverlays at line 322).

NGA emits horizontal lines only at each cell's south edge (GridZone.swift:160-179). So the northing line at upperNorthing, and the cells above it, only exist after a rebuild. The coverage square has only 43 pt of vertical margin. At z18 (0.47 m/pt) a pan of up to about 111 m (0.001 deg) with no rebuild can expose about 190 pt with no northing line or verticals. A PDF/blank source allows zoom up to 22 (TileMapView.swift:161-162), so z18+ is reachable.

The auditor's proving test is flawed: 37.8129 + 0.0009 = 37.8138 crosses into the '37.814' bucket and would trigger a rebuild. Use e.g. 37.8126 to 37.8134 instead.

There is no zone clip in either renderer (MGRSGridRenderer.swift:74-115; MgrsGridRenderer.kt:84-120). NGA drawBounds floors/ceils past the zone edge (GridZone.swift:291-324), and only the horizontal segment gets a bounds point.

The auditor understates the geometry. GridZone.swift:160-176 reassigns `southwest` to the westBoundsPoint BEFORE appending the vertical line, so the vertical segment runs from about 12E to the original NW point and is a diagonal.

The real jar, for bounds 47.95-48.1N, 11.9-12.1E, gives zone-33 segments entirely west of 12E: 18 (1 km), 4 (10 km), 2 (100 km). Examples:
- 100 km: (47.8141N, 11.9999E) -> (48.6809N, 10.9240E), about 37 deg off vertical.
- 10 km: (47.9041, 12.0000) -> (47.9919, 11.9170).

These look like a sawtooth of diagonal lines along the zone boundary, not a 4.5 deg tilt. The core claim stands.

HUNDRED_KILOMETER is added unconditionally (MGRSGridRenderer.swift:65-68; MgrsGridRenderer.kt:73-77), and iOS starts at zoom 4 (TileMapContainer.swift:85). With the real jar, for a 393x852 coverage square at 38N the 100 km type alone gives:
- z4: 15,026 segments, 29.5 ms.
- z2: 99,804 segments, 105 ms.

That is before the per-segment MGRS.from label calls. 100 km spacing at z4 at 38N is about 13 pt.

Rebuild frequency:
- iOS: rebuilds whenever the %.3f span changes, i.e. every pinch frame at low zoom.
- Android: rebuilds on every camera change.

Both run on the main thread.

Both platforms cap the raster at scale 1 (1 px per PDF pt):
- iOS: boundedPDFRasterSize min(1, ...) (PDFOverlay.swift:68-88), used by PDFMapSource.renderedImage (PDFMapSource.swift:96).
- Android: boundedPdfRenderSize minOf(1.0, ...) (PdfPageRenderer.kt:44-60, 77-91).

At 1:24k, 1 pt is 8.47 m. At z18 at 37.8N (0.472 m/pt) one image pixel covers about 18 pt.

Android's PdfTiler.zoomRange uses floor(log2(pageWidth/lonSpan*360/256)) (PdfTiler.kt:208-216). With 1728 px over about 0.17 deg that is z13. The iOS zoomRange fills a 2500-tile budget, which reaches about z16 for the sample.

GeoPdfParser correspondences are absolute user-space coordinates (bx0 + nx*dx, GeoPdfParser.kt:210-215). PdfGroundLayer maps the bitmap corners to transform(0,ph)...transform(0,0), with pw/ph taken from PdfRenderer's pageInfo (CustomMapOverlays.kt:858-865). pageRectForBand flips with h - y (PdfTiler.kt:186-194), and pdfPointFor also assumes origin 0.

PdfRenderer (PDFium) reports and renders the CropBox bbox, and Page.getWidth/getHeight are Int (truncated). preflightPdfImport (MapScreenHelpers.kt:424-439) does no crop-origin check.

So a CropBox [36 36 ...] shifts the whole sheet by 36 pt, and a fractional size misplaces the far edges by up to 1 pt. The sample ([0 0 1728 2088]) is unaffected.

iOS draws each tile with frame.insetBy(dx:-0.5, dy:-0.5) (TileMapView.swift:84-89), a symmetric 0.5 pt growth that displaces edge content by up to 0.5 pt. Android rounds x, y and edge independently after a 0.5 dp inflate (TileMapView.kt:203-213), giving up to about 0.5 dp + 1 px of mismatch that changes as the zoom varies. This only affects raster tiles (baked MBTiles or basemaps), not the live PDF overlay. It is sub-metre at z18 but visible as a 1 px shimmer. Low is correct.

verify.missed:
1) D4-12 is worse than described (both platforms, via vendored NGA). ios/Vendor/mgrs-ios/mgrs-ios/gzd/GridZone.swift:160-176 (the same in the mgrs-2.1.3 jar) replaces `southwest` with the zone-edge bounds point before appending the 'vertical' line. As a result, every first-column vertical segment in a zone is a DIAGONAL from about the zone boundary to the original NW corner, not a slightly tilted line. Verified with the jar:
- 100 km: (47.8141N, 11.9999E) -> (48.6809N, 10.9240E), about 37 deg off vertical.
- 10 km: (47.9041, 12.0) -> (47.9919, 11.917).
Since 100 km lines are always on, every view near a 6-degree zone boundary shows a sawtooth of long diagonals. The fix is the same as D4-12 (clip to the zone polygon before drawing).

2) Duplicate grid segments at 8-degree latitude band boundaries (both platforms), low severity. GridZones.zones/getZones returns one GridZone per (zone, band) (MGRSGridRenderer.swift:62-77; MgrsGridRenderer.kt:80-87). Each band's drawBounds is floored/ceiled past the band's latitude limit, and NGA never clips latitude. So when the view straddles a band edge (e.g. 48N), the same 100 km cell lines are emitted twice, and the 1 km/10 km row at the band boundary is emitted twice. The jar showed each 100 km zone-33 segment listed twice for 47.95-48.1N. Consequences:
- The duplicates are stroked twice with 0.85-alpha ink, so the line looks darker/heavier.
- Build and draw cost doubles for that row.
Test: build for 47.95-48.1N, 8.5-8.7E and assert no two segments share both endpoints.

audit.summary:
How the import works. iOS: Menu > Import PDF Map > .fileImporter([.pdf]) > handleImport (ContentView.swift:1946). ImportedMapWorker.preparePDF runs detached. It does a security-scoped coordinated read, then a chunked, cancellable, size-capped (512 MB) copy that refuses symlinks, into Application Support/ImportedMaps with CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication protection. It then checks the PDF with PDFKit (not locked, page 0 exists), reads bounds with GeoPDFReader (CGPDF dictionaries) and takes a SHA-256 content key. Back on the main actor it builds a PDFMapSource (camera-centred fallback if there is no georef), reapplies any sealed manual calibration found by content hash, and calls MapViewModel.selectMapSource. That saves the sealed PDF session and the SafeStore selector (active + one retained map), publishes, and deletes every other managed map file. TileMapContainer.syncPDF then rasterises page 0 (max 4096 px / 32 MB) and warps it through the placement affine.

Android: ImportExportSheet > an OpenDocument picker owned by the Activity > the pending import is saved in prefs > MapScreen LaunchedEffect. On the IO thread, IdempotentDocumentCopy writes a journaled .partial, fsyncs, does an atomic move and caps at 256 MB. Preflight reads the page size with PdfRenderer and rejects any /Rotate via PDFBox. GeoPdfParser (PDFBox) builds correspondences and AffineFitter fits them, otherwise the fallback box is used. On the main thread vm.setMapSource saves the sealed PdfSessionStore and the ActiveMapSelectionStore, then reconciles files. PdfGroundLayer renders the bitmap on IO and warps it with setPolyToPoly.

What is solid on both platforms:
- Crash-safe copy: bounded and cancellable on iOS, journaled and idempotent on Android.
- State is saved before it is shown, with exact rollback if the save fails.
- File cleanup does not follow symlinks and removes crash leftovers (.partial, -wal).
- Calibrations are tied to the file's content hash, and the sidecars are sealed.
- Raster sizes and metadata entry counts are capped; password-protected PDFs are rejected.
- Offline tiles are baked to a .partial file and only published on success.
- Android disables backups.

Where it breaks:
1. The fail-closed LPTS range check added in commit 1c023de rejects the repo's own USGS US Topo sample, so it is imported silently as an unplaced PDF. This is the most likely cause of 'the grid doesn't line up'.
2. Every PDF without accepted georef is shown as a normal 'Offline basemap' at a made-up location, with no warning.
3. The library holds only one map: importing a second map, or baking tiles, silently deletes the earlier PDF.
4. Android's 'Unload' buttons delete files with no confirmation.
5. The PDF is saved before it is first rendered, so a PDF that crashes the renderer crash-loops the app on every launch.
6. iOS rasterises and re-hashes on the main thread.
7. The calibration session is not tied to its source PDF, and rotation, multi-page files and iOS backups are handled differently on each platform.

findings.title: Hardening regression: the reference USGS US Topo GeoPDF is rejected and imported as an unplaced PDF on both platforms
findings.description: Commit 1c023de made both parsers reject any viewport whose LPTS values fall outside [0,1] (iOS GeoPDFReader.swift:349; Android GeoPdfParser.kt:206). Before that, any value was accepted. USGS US Topo writes its map-body viewport ('Map Layers', BBox [0 2088 1727.96 56.69], Measure obj 424) with LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514], because the neatline corners sit just outside the BBox. I confirmed this by decoding the object streams of samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf. The largest viewport is now 'malformed', so the rule that a larger malformed GEO viewport overrides a smaller valid inset returns Rejected for the whole page (iOS :220-224 then nil at :84-85; Android :232-236 then null at :78). The sample has no LGIDict to fall back on. Both importers then use the camera-centred 10 km fallback (ContentView.swift:1962; MapScreenHelpers.kt:495). Replaying both selection routines on the real values (scratchpad/audit/vp_select.py): Map Layers 3,510,016 pt² is malformed, the best valid inset is 5,006 pt², so the result is REJECTED. If the viewport were accepted, a 4-point affine fits with a residual of 9e-5 degrees or less, so the data itself is fine. The unit tests on both platforms enshrine '1.1 = malformed'. The seeded-USGS screenshot UI test only waits for the 'Map' button, which also appears for a fallback import, so the regression went unnoticed.
findings.failure_scenario: Import samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf (or any current US Topo quad) on iPhone or Android. The whole 24x29 in page, including the collar, is stretched into a 10 km box around wherever the camera was. On iOS the box is square, so the aspect ratio is also distorted. The printed 1000 m UTM grid is kilometres away from the MGRS overlay, and the UI calls the result a normal offline basemap.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept any finite LPTS value (or a generous tolerance such as [-0.5, 1.5]). Use AffineFitter's residual, crossValidated flag and a maximum-RMS gate as the fail-closed test instead. Keep the 'malformed map body overrides inset' rule only for non-finite or structurally broken entries. Add a shared testdata/ fixture containing the exact USGS viewport triple, used by both test suites.
findings.proving_test: Shared-fixture test on both platforms: build a raw PDF with the three USGS viewports (BBoxes and GPTS/LPTS as in the sample) and call GeoPDFReader.bounds / GeoPdfParser.parse. Expect non-nil bounds with SW about (37.7324, -122.5212) and NE about (37.8890, -122.3526) to 1e-4, and kind == geoPDF. Add an opt-in test that parses samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf when the file is present. Both currently return nil.

findings.title: PDFs without accepted georeferencing are silently shown as a valid basemap at a made-up location
findings.description:
Any PDF without accepted georeferencing is published as a real basemap at a location invented from the camera centre. This covers plain PDFs, GeoPDFs whose metadata was rejected or is unsupported (D5-01), and georeferencing on page 2 or later (D5-13). iOS uses a 10 km square with no placement affine, so the page is stretched out of aspect. Android uses a 10 km-tall box that keeps the aspect ratio. So each platform is wrong in a different way. Nothing tells the user:
- iOS shows no message at all.
- Android toasts 'Imported X'.
- Both headers show the green 'Offline basemap' label, and the MGRS grid and coordinate readout draw on top.
- The iOS Layers sheet calls it 'Manually placed bounds'. The 'No georeferencing' label can never appear, because bounds are never nil after import.
The fake placement is saved and restored on every relaunch. A rejected GeoPDF looks exactly like a plain PDF.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports a scanned 1:50k sheet (or a USGS quad, see D5-01) while standing in the area. The sheet appears centred on them with the MGRS grid on top. They put the crosshair on a hilltop on the PDF and read off a grid reference that is kilometres wrong. Nothing on screen says the sheet is not registered.
findings.suggested_fix: Model the georef state explicitly: georeferenced, manually calibrated, unregistered, or metadata rejected. For unregistered or rejected sheets, show a persistent red 'NOT GEOREFERENCED - calibrate before use' banner and an amber basemap label. Prompt for calibration right after import, and for rejected metadata explain that georeferencing was found but is invalid or unsupported. Use one aspect-preserving fallback on both platforms. Fix the iOS label logic.
findings.proving_test: Import a generated plain PDF through the production path on each platform. Assert the source reports the unregistered state, a warning message or banner is published, and the header label is not 'Offline basemap'. Add a UI test that looks for the banner text after import.

findings.title: Importing a second map (or any MBTiles) silently deletes the previous imported map and any tiles baked from it
findings.description: The selector keeps exactly one retained imported map. Every successful selection runs a reconcile that unlinks every other managed .pdf or .mbtiles under ImportedMaps/offline_tiles (iOS) or pdf_maps/mbtiles/offline_tiles (Android). Tests enshrine this behaviour. The import flows show no warning. The iOS Layers text even tells the user the retained map is 'Saved locally and available'. A multi-sheet area of operations cannot be held on the device. Importing sheet B deletes sheet A's private copy and any MBTiles baked from A, which can be minutes of work. Only a manual calibration survives, keyed by content hash, and only if the original file can be found and imported again.
findings.failure_scenario: A patrol spans two adjacent 1:25k sheets. The user imports and calibrates sheet A, bakes tiles, then imports sheet B. A's PDF and tiles are unlinked immediately with no prompt. In the field the original attachment or USB copy is gone, so A cannot be recovered.
findings.suggested_fix: Until there is a multi-entry library (listed as an extension point in ARCHITECTURE.md), confirm before replacing: 'Importing B removes A (and its offline tiles) from this device'. Offer Cancel. Better, allow N retained maps with an explicit Delete for each.
findings.proving_test: View-model test on each platform: select PDF A, then select PDF B through selectMapSource/setMapSource. Assert that a confirmation is requested before A's file is removed. Today FileManager/File.exists(A) becomes false synchronously with no prompt.

findings.title: Android 'Unload PDF Map' / 'Unload Offline Tiles' permanently delete the files with no confirmation
findings.description: The 'Unload' buttons call vm.unloadPdfMap() / unloadOfflineTiles() directly. Both pass clearRetained=true, which leads to saveOnlineAndClearRetained, and the reconcile then runs with an empty keep set. That deletes every file in pdf_maps/, mbtiles/ and offline_tiles/ and clears the PDF session. There is no dialog and no undo, and the word 'Unload' suggests nothing is deleted. iOS splits this into a non-destructive 'Switch to Online Basemap' and a destructive 'Delete PDF Map…' / 'Delete Offline Map…' behind a confirmation alert.
findings.failure_scenario: A user wants to glance at satellite imagery and taps 'Unload Offline Tiles'. A 2 GB imported MBTiles pack, or a PDF plus its baked tiles, is deleted instantly and cannot be re-copied in the field.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the buttons to 'Delete …' and add the same destructive confirmation as iOS. Add a non-destructive 'Switch to online basemap' button; selectBaseMap already keeps the retained map.
findings.proving_test: Compose UI test: load an MBTiles fixture, open Layers and tap 'Unload Offline Tiles'. Expect a confirmation dialog, and assert the file under filesDir/mbtiles still exists before confirming. Today it is deleted synchronously.

findings.title: 'Generate Offline Tiles' deletes the source PDF; on Android the result is also lower resolution than the PDF
findings.description: When a bake finishes, the MBTiles becomes the active and retained map. The reconcile then clears the PDF session and unlinks the PDF on both platforms. The UI text ('Bakes this calibrated map into an offline tile set') never says the PDF will be removed. After a bake the user cannot recalibrate, re-bake, or go back to the vector PDF. Android also picks maxZoom from page points, treating 1 pt as 1 px (72 dpi): pxPerDeg = pageWidth / lonSpan. For the USGS 1:24k sheet that is z13, about 15.1 m/px at 37.8N. That is coarser than the live PDF overlay (about 8.5 m/px) and far below iOS's z16 (about 1.9 m/px under its 2,500-tile budget); see scratchpad/audit/bake_zoom.py. So on Android the bake is a visible quality downgrade that also cannot be undone.
findings.failure_scenario: An Android user bakes the calibrated USGS quad 'for offline use'. Beyond z13 the map goes blurry and contour labels become unreadable. The PDF is already deleted, so the only way back is to import it again from the original file.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the PDF: retain both entries, or make the bake add a new entry instead of replacing. Say explicitly what will happen. On Android, derive maxZoom from a target resolution (for example 200-300 dpi equivalent, capped by the tile budget) or reuse the iOS zoom-range logic.
findings.proving_test: Instrumented/XCTest: bake a calibrated fixture through the production UI path, then assert the source PDF still exists and can still be selected. Android unit test of PdfTiler.zoomRange for a 1728 pt page spanning 0.169 degrees: expect maxZoom >= 15 (it returns 13 today).

findings.title: Bake task lifecycle: iOS orphaned background bake can switch maps and delete a newer import; Android cannot cancel; failure messages are wrong
findings.description:
iOS:
- The bake is a Task.detached held only in LayersSheet @State, with no cancel when the sheet goes away.
- Progress and Cancel exist only inside the sheet. If the sheet is dismissed, both are lost; reopening it offers 'Generate Offline Tiles…' again, so a second bake can run at the same time.
- When the orphaned task finishes it calls mapVM.selectMapSource, which switches the basemap unexpectedly and, through reconcile, deletes whatever PDF the user imported in the meantime.
- No background-task assertion is taken, so auto-lock suspends the bake.
- The button is offered for every PDF. PDFTiler returns nil when there is no placement transform (uncalibrated PDF or known-sheet PDF), and the user is then told to 'check free storage'.

Android:
- The progress dialog is modal and cannot be dismissed. It has no Cancel, even though PdfTiler honours cancellation.
- Each tile reopens the file and creates a new PdfRenderer, so a 2,500-tile bake can take minutes.
- Every failure, including disk-full and render errors, reports 'calibrate the PDF first'.
findings.failure_scenario: iOS: start baking sheet A, swipe the sheet away, then import sheet B. When A's bake finishes, tiles(A) become active and B is deleted. Android: the user notices they started a bake on the wrong PDF and must wait minutes with no way out.
findings.suggested_fix: Move bake ownership into MapViewModel (or an app-level service) with persistent progress and Cancel. Refuse to publish if the active source changed while baking. Take a UIApplication background task on iOS. Add a Cancel button on Android. Return typed errors and show accurate messages. Disable the button for unregistered PDFs.
findings.proving_test: iOS: start a bake through a coordinator, set mapVM.mapSource to a different PDF, and let the bake complete. Assert the new PDF is still active and its file still exists. Android Compose test: the bake dialog exposes Cancel, and cancelling removes offline_tiles/*.partial.

findings.title: Crash loop: the PDF is saved before it is ever rendered, and every launch auto-renders it with no crash-loop breaker
findings.description:
Import preflight only opens page 0 and reads its size; it never draws the page. The first real render happens after the source has been durably selected. On iOS that render runs on the main thread inside updateUIView; on Android it runs as PdfGroundLayer on IO. Every cold start restores the active PDF and renders it again automatically, and nothing records that a render is in progress. If drawing the page kills the process, the app dies again on every launch before the user can reach Layers. Ways the render can kill the process:
- iOS jetsam while decoding a huge embedded scan or JPX image.
- Android pdfium's allocation-failure abort.
- A native crash in pdfium on malformed content.
Android also persists the picker result and replays the import automatically after process death. A crash inside preflight therefore loops too. A repo-wide search found no crash-loop detection on either platform.
findings.failure_scenario: Import a 600 dpi A0 scan, one image of about 20k x 28k pixels. The process is killed during the first draw, and every later launch is killed the same way. The only way out is deleting the app, which on iOS also destroys mission data sealed with the ThisDeviceOnly key.
findings.suggested_fix: Write a 'render in progress' marker (keyed by content hash) before the first render and before cold-start renders, and clear it on success. At launch, if the marker is still present, restore the online basemap instead and show 'TacMap closed while drawing <map> - Open anyway / Remove'. Render a low-resolution probe inside the import worker before saving. Cap automatic retries of the pending import on Android.
findings.proving_test: Inject a renderer that never completes (leaving the marker set) and run a cold restoreActiveMapSelection / MapViewModel init. It must publish the online source and a recovery issue rather than the PDF. On Android, simulate process death with a pending import whose preflight throws Error and assert it is not retried more than N times.

findings.title: Main-thread work: iOS rasterises the page and re-hashes the whole PDF many times on the UI thread; Android hashes on main when saving
findings.description:
iOS:
- The renderer calls pdf.renderedImage() synchronously inside updateUIView, even though PDFMapSource documents that call as heavy and off-main only. The page is rasterised on the main thread on import, on every launch, and on every switch back to the PDF.
- PDFSessionStore.load hashes the whole file twice (resolveImportedMap at :291-294, then again at :177).
- load runs on main during restore, during the reconcile after every successful selection (including switching between online styles), and during LayersSheet onAppear and refreshRetainedMap. Opening Layers and tapping one online style while a PDF is retained costs about 8-10 full-file SHA-256 passes on main.

Android:
- PdfSessionStore.save hashes the file on the main thread for every Fiduciaries source.
- Every auto-parsed GeoPDF is stored as Fiduciaries (PdfMapSource.calibrated), so this happens on every GeoPDF import and every calibration, followed by fsync'd SafeStore writes, all on Main.
findings.failure_scenario: With a 400 MB scanned PDF on iPhone, the UI freezes for several seconds after import, on every launch, and on each basemap tap in Layers. Rasterising a heavy USGS page with 168 DCT image tiles blocks input on its own. On a mid-range Android phone, a 256 MB GeoPDF import freezes the UI for about a second after the 'Imported' toast.
findings.suggested_fix: Render in a detached task and attach the image when ready; cachedRenderedImage already exists for this. Cache the verified content key per (inode, size, mtime), or verify once off-main at restore. Move the Android save and hash work to Dispatchers.IO before the publication step.
findings.proving_test: XCTest: drive Coordinator.syncPDF with a PDFMapSource whose rasteriser records Thread.isMainThread, and expect false. Count PDFSessionStore.contentKey calls across restoreRetainedMapSelection() + selectOnlineBasemap(); expect at most 1 (currently 8 or more). Android: StrictMode/Looper test that setMapSource(pdf) does no file reads on Main.

findings.title: No progress or cancel for PDF import on either platform; Android parses the untrusted PDF three times
findings.description:
Neither platform shows any in-progress state after the picker closes; iOS importWorkTask is never bound to UI. Android runs these steps with no feedback, for files up to 256 MB:
1. A bounded copy loop that cannot be cancelled.
2. PdfRenderer open plus a full PDFBox load inside validate.
3. The same preflight again, which is a second PdfRenderer and a second PDFBox load.
4. GeoPdfParser.parse, a third PDFBox load.
If the user picks again during this time, Android revokes the first URI grant while that copy is still running. iOS silently cancels the first import.
findings.failure_scenario: A 200 MB PDF from a USB-OTG stick gives 10-30 s with nothing on screen. The user re-imports, and the first attempt ends in a confusing failure toast or silently disappears.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a progress HUD with Cancel. Do a single parse pass that returns page info, rotation and georef together. Check for cancellation cooperatively inside the copy loop.
findings.proving_test: UI test: after picking a large fixture, an 'Importing…' indicator with Cancel must appear within 500 ms. Android unit test counting PDDocument.load calls per importPdfMapSource: expect 1 (currently 3).

findings.title: Calibration session is not tied to the PDF being calibrated: Android applies sheet A's fiduciaries to sheet B and saves them permanently
findings.description:
Android:
- Calibration state is reset only when the new source is not a PdfMapSource (MapScreen.kt:709-715).
- The Import/Export menu is still reachable while calibrating.
- If the user imports PDF B in the middle of calibrating A, A's fiduciaries (A's page coordinates and MGRS strings) survive.
- Finish fits them and applies the result to the current pdfSource, which is B. It is saved, and saveToLibrary writes it under B's content hash as a 'manual' calibration.
- On re-import, a manual calibration takes precedence over GeoPDF parsing, so B stays misplaced even if B is a valid GeoPDF. Neither platform has a 'reset calibration' action.

iOS:
- CalibrationSession holds its source weakly and is never cancelled when the map source changes.
- After importing B, taps keep recording points on B's overlay next to A's markers.
- Finish then does nothing, because the weak source is gone and the guard returns silently.
findings.failure_scenario: The user starts calibrating sheet A, realises it is the wrong sheet, imports B and taps Finish. On Android, B is placed using A's control points, and that placement is saved to B's content hash for good. On iOS, the Finish button does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Cancel the calibration (with a confirmation) on any change of map source, or tie the session to a source id and refuse to finish on a mismatch. Hide import while calibrating. Add 'Reset calibration', which removes the content-hash library entry and restores GeoPDF parsing.
findings.proving_test: Android VM/Compose test: startPdfCalibration on A, add 3 fiduciaries, setMapSource(B), then call finishPdfCalibration. Assert B is not calibrated with A's fiduciaries and PdfSessionStore.calibration(fileB) == null. iOS: same sequence; assert calibration.isCalibrating becomes false when the source changes.

findings.title: Calibration Finish: silent no-ops, a misleading 'could not be saved' error, a success toast after failure, and no feedback on fit quality
findings.description:
iOS:
- A degenerate or collinear fit is swallowed (print) in CalibrationSession.finish, and ContentView.finishCalibration returns silently, so Finish looks dead.
- If the fit succeeds but applyCalibration rejects it (a page corner off the Earth, or a non-invertible affine), the new source has bounds == nil. PDFSessionStore.save then returns false, and the user sees 'The PDF map could not be saved for relaunch' with a Retry that can never succeed.
- The RMS is never shown: finish() sets lastFitRMSMetres, then cancel() immediately clears it.

Android:
- calibrated() returns the source unchanged when validation fails, setMapSource succeeds, and a 'Calibration RMS Xm' success toast appears even though nothing was applied.
- The entered fiduciaries are lost, because the next session seeds from source.calibration.

Both platforms:
- With 3 points the affine is exact, so any typo is absorbed with 0 RMS.
- With 4 or more points the RMS is only a transient toast (Android) or hidden (iOS).
- There is no threshold and no outlier check.
findings.failure_scenario: The user mistypes one MGRS zone (10S instead of 18S). With 3 points, Android shows a success toast while the sheet stays at the fallback place; iOS shows a persistence error. With 4 points and a 1 km digit swap, the RMS of about 400 m flashes for 2 s (Android) or never appears (iOS), and the misregistered sheet goes live.
findings.suggested_fix: Return typed fit and validation errors with actionable text. Show the RMS and per-point residuals before applying. Warn or block above a scale-dependent threshold. Encourage 4 or more points and flag leave-one-out outliers.
findings.proving_test: iOS: CalibrationSession with 3 collinear fiduciaries, then finishCalibration must publish an error message, and a successful fit must leave the RMS visible. Android: finishPdfCalibration with fiduciaries whose affine maps a page corner beyond 90 degrees latitude must show an error and must not toast the RMS.

findings.title: Rotated pages: Android refuses them and tells the user to use a desktop; iOS accepts them with no orientation handling
findings.description: Android rejects any /Rotate other than 0. It also rejects any PDF that PDFBox cannot open to inspect rotation, even when pdfium renders it fine, and the message points the user to 'flatten or print it to a new PDF'. That is a desktop-only remedy for a field user; phone-scanned landscape maps commonly carry /Rotate 90. iOS accepts rotated pages, and its test only checks that the raster is non-empty. There is no rotation logic: the rasteriser and tiler draw with page.draw(with: .mediaBox, to:) into a context sized and cropped to the unrotated mediaBox or crop rect. GeoPDF LPTS/Neatline coordinates and calibration taps, however, are in unrotated user space. PDFKit's bounds(for:) ignores rotation, while draw applies the page display transform, so rotated content is likely drawn rotated or clipped relative to the geometry. Nothing verifies which. The same file is refused on Android and imported, possibly misplaced, on iOS.
findings.failure_scenario: A /Rotate 90 GeoPDF or scanned landscape map: Android says 'flatten or print it'; iOS imports it with unverified orientation and registration.
findings.suggested_fix: Support /Rotate: keep all georef and calibration maths in unrotated user space and render unrotated. On iOS, use CGContext.drawPDFPage without the display transform, or counter-rotate. On Android, prepend the inverse of pdfium's rotation to the render matrix. For manual calibration, show the page as viewers display it and map taps back through the rotation. Until that exists, make both platforms behave the same, and give a message that distinguishes 'PDFBox could not parse' from rotation.
findings.proving_test: Shared fixture: a /Rotate 90 page with a filled square at user space (50,50)-(100,100) and an LL LGIDict. Render it through each platform's rasteriser and assert the dark pixels land where the placement affine projects (75,75). Assert Android preflight accepts it once rotation is supported.

findings.title: Multi-page PDFs silently use page 1 only; georeferencing on later pages is ignored
findings.description: Import, the geo parser, the rasteriser and the tiler all hard-code page 0 on both platforms. There is no page picker and no notice when pageCount > 1. A GeoPDF whose map is on page 2 (a legend or cover first, or map books and atlases) is imported as page 1. Its /VP or LGIDict is ignored; a catalog-level /VP is used only when page 1 has none. The result then falls into the silent camera-centred fallback (D5-02).
findings.failure_scenario: A 2-page GeoPDF with the legend on page 1 and the map on page 2: the legend page is placed over the user's location and shown as the offline basemap.
findings.suggested_fix: When pageCount > 1, show a page picker with thumbnails and highlight pages that carry /VP or /LGIDict. Save the page index in the session and use it for render, parse and bake.
findings.proving_test: Fixture: page 1 plain, page 2 with a valid /VP. Import must either prompt for a page or pick page 2 and return georeferenced bounds. Currently it returns the fallback on both platforms.

findings.title: iOS: plaintext imported maps (saved under their original file names) are included in iCloud and Finder backups; Android excludes them
findings.description: iOS copies imported PDFs into Application Support/ImportedMaps under the user's original file name, and writes baked tiles to Application Support/offline_tiles. No code under ios/ sets isExcludedFromBackup, so both are backed up by default as plaintext. Mission data, by contrast, is sealed with a ThisDeviceOnly key that does not migrate. Android disables cloud backup and device transfer entirely and uses opaque import-<hash>.pdf names. THREAT_MODEL.md only discusses filesystem extraction and file-sharing exposure; it does not mention backup upload.
findings.failure_scenario: A user imports 'AO_<area>_1-25k.pdf'. iCloud Backup uploads the plaintext sheet and its revealing file name. Restoring that backup elsewhere yields the area-of-interest map, even though the waypoints stay unreadable.
findings.suggested_fix: Set isExcludedFromBackup on the ImportedMaps and offline_tiles directories and on every file written into them. Store the files under opaque names and keep the display name in the sealed session. Document the behaviour in THREAT_MODEL.
findings.proving_test: XCTest: after ImportedMapFileCopier.copyToImportedMaps and after a PDFTiler bake, assert resourceValues(forKeys:[.isExcludedFromBackupKey]).isExcludedFromBackup == true and that the stored file name does not contain the source file's stem.

findings.title: Untrusted PDFs are parsed with no memory or time budget; Android swallows OutOfMemoryError and StackOverflowError; the threat model omits imported maps
findings.description: Android loads the untrusted PDF with PdfBox-Android 2.0.27 using PDDocument.load(file), three times per import. The default scratch setting is main-memory only, so object streams and filtered streams are fully inflated in the Java heap when dereferenced. There is no cap on decoded size and no timeout. runCatching catches Throwable, which includes OutOfMemoryError and StackOverflowError, under largeHeap. A Flate bomb in the object stream holding the page dictionary therefore thrashes or exhausts the heap. An OOM thrown on another thread (UI or renderer) can crash the app, and if the process survives the user sees the misleading 'could not safely inspect page rotation'. pdfium (PdfRenderer) runs in-process, and iOS relies on CGPDF/PDFKit with no budget. THREAT_MODEL's trust-boundary table lists imported symbol packs as untrusted but not imported PDFs or MBTiles, which are the largest parser attack surface.
findings.failure_scenario: A crafted 2 MB PDF whose page object sits in an object stream that inflates to 1 GB: Android import stalls under GC thrash, and the app may be killed by OOM on the main thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Use MemoryUsageSetting.setupMixed(small main-memory budget) with a maximum storage cap. Parse once, with a watchdog timeout. Do not catch Error subclasses; fail the import cleanly. Consider moving PDFBox and PdfRenderer work into an isolatedProcess service. Add 'Imported PDF/GeoPDF/MBTiles - Untrusted' to THREAT_MODEL §3.
findings.proving_test: Instrumented test: generate an object-stream bomb (Flate of 512 MB of zeros holding the Page dictionary). Call preflightPdfImport and GeoPdfParser.parse; they must fail within a few seconds with a Java heap delta under 64 MB and a specific 'PDF too complex' error.

findings.title: Render failures are silent: blank map under a green 'Offline basemap' label; iOS retries the render on every UI update
findings.description: Android: PdfGroundLayer catches any render exception and does nothing, so the PDF stays the active basemap with nothing drawn. iOS: when renderedImage() returns nil (for example a zero-area crop or media box, or a document that cannot be opened), syncPDF silently removes the overlay and the dark mask. Because the failure is not cached, every later updateUIView, including each camera publish during a pan, re-opens the PDFDocument and tries again on the main thread.
findings.failure_scenario: A PDF with a degenerate page box or a render error: the user sees an empty map labelled 'Offline basemap' with no explanation, and iOS panning stutters while it keeps re-parsing.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface a render error and fall back to the last or an online basemap. Cache the failure per source id.
findings.proving_test: iOS: PDFMapSource with a zero-area crop; call syncPDF twice and assert PDFRasteriser.render runs once and an error is published. Android: PdfGroundLayer with a renderer that throws must emit an error state.

findings.title: iOS 'Imported Map' visibility toggle does nothing
findings.description: The Layers sheet binds a Toggle to visibility.pdfOverlayVisible and saves it, but nothing in the custom renderer reads it. syncPDF always attaches the PDF image and mask. The switch appears to hide the sheet but has no effect; it is a leftover from the removed MKMapView path.
findings.failure_scenario: A user switches the imported map off to compare with another layer, and the PDF stays on screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Honour the flag in TileMapContainer.syncPDF (hide both pdfView and pdfMask), or remove the control.
findings.proving_test: XCTest: set visibility.pdfOverlayVisible = false, run updateUIView, and assert the PDFImageOverlayView is hidden or absent.

findings.title: Android saves the picked document URI (often including the area-of-interest file name) in plaintext SharedPreferences during import
findings.description: persistPendingDocumentImport writes the content URI to pending_document_import_v1 in plaintext. For ExternalStorageProvider that URI embeds the path, for example primary%3ADownload%2F<name>.pdf. The URI stays there until the import finishes, and stays indefinitely if the import keeps crashing (D5-07). The app's own policy says imported file names can identify an area of operations and must live in SafeStore; the map selector follows that rule, this handoff does not.
findings.failure_scenario: An import of 'Download/AO_<area>.pdf' crashes. The plaintext prefs XML keeps the path until the next successful import, and it is readable by anyone with filesystem-level access.
findings.suggested_fix: Seal the pending-import record with SafeStore, as the copy journal already is, or save only an opaque token and keep the URI in memory plus savedInstanceState.
findings.proving_test: Robolectric test: call receiveDocumentImportResult with a URI containing 'AO_Test.pdf', then read the raw shared_prefs XML and assert it does not contain 'AO_Test'.

findings.title: Deleting an imported map keeps its calibration (control-point coordinates, MGRS and labels) in the sealed library indefinitely
findings.description: Delete and Unload clear only the active PDF session. The per-content-hash calibration library is never pruned on either platform and has no UI to clear it. It keeps the fiduciary lat/lon, MGRS strings and user labels such as 'Church spire'. The iOS delete dialog tells the user the map is removed 'from the map library'. The data is sealed, but it outlives what the user was told was deleted.
findings.failure_scenario: The user deletes a mission's PDF before handing the device on. The operating area's control points remain in the sealed store, readable to anyone who later unlocks mission data on that device.
findings.suggested_fix: When deleting a retained PDF, also remove its content-hash library entry; the hash is known from the session. Offer a 'Clear saved calibrations' action, and describe the behaviour in THREAT_MODEL.
findings.proving_test: Calibrate PDF A, delete it through the production delete or unload path, then assert PDFSessionStore / PdfSessionStore no longer returns a calibration for A's bytes.

findings.title: Import limits and rejection messages differ between platforms
findings.description: iOS accepts PDFs up to 512 MB; Android caps at 256 MB, and its message hard-codes that figure. On iOS, an oversized file surfaces as a raw CocoaError(.fileReadTooLarge) string. A password-protected PDF gets the generic 'Couldn't import this file as a valid PDF' on iOS, while Android says 'may be invalid or password-protected'. Neither platform offers to unlock it.
findings.failure_scenario: A team shares a 300 MB scanned sheet. It imports on the iPhones and fails on the Android devices; locked PDFs produce different, unclear messages on each platform.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one size cap and one set of message keys across platforms. Add a distinct 'password-protected' message on iOS, and optionally an unlock prompt using PDFDocument.unlock / PdfRenderer with a decrypted copy.
findings.proving_test: Cross-platform contract test in testdata/: the limit constants must match, and a locked-PDF fixture must produce the same message key on both platforms.

verdicts.reasoning:
I decoded the sample's object streams myself. Measure 424 (the 'Map Layers' viewport, BBox [0 2088 1727.96 56.69]) has LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514]. Its GCS 425 is NAD83 UTM 10N. There is no LGIDict anywhere in the file.

Root cause:
- iOS viewportAffine requires every LPTS value to be in [0,1] (GeoPDFReader.swift:347-350), so the map body falls into largestMalformedDeclaredGeoArea (:210-212).
- Android does the same at GeoPdfParser.kt:205-209.
- The only valid candidates are the 'Quadrangle Location' inset (83.5 x 59.9 = 5,006 pt^2, a state-scale locator) and the adjoining-sheet diagram (3,336 pt^2).
- The 3,510,016 pt^2 malformed map body is larger than 5,006, so both parsers return Rejected (iOS :218-222; Android :232-236). iOS then returns nil at :84-85 before LGIDict or known sheets, and Android returns null at :78.
- Both importers fall back to camera-centred bounds (ContentView.swift:1962; MapScreenHelpers.kt:495 returns base = PdfMapSource.imported fallback).

`git log -S` confirms both range checks were introduced in 1c023de. My own lstsq fit of the 4 correspondences gives lat residual about 0 and lon residual ±9.0e-5 deg, so the data is usable.

The tests enshrine '1.1 = malformed' (PDFImportSmokeTests.swift:204/339; PdfImportHardeningInstrumentedTest.kt:326-329). Note the 'malformed body overrides inset' rule is itself correct: without it the California-scale inset would have been chosen. The bug is the [0,1] range test.

Placement:
- iOS handleImport uses GeoPDFReader.fallbackBounds (ContentView.swift:1962). That is a 10 km lat/lon square with no placementAffine (GeoPDFReader.swift:858-895), so PDFImageOverlayView stretches the page out of aspect.
- Android PdfMapSource.imported/fallbackBounds keeps the aspect ratio (PdfMapSource.kt:43-71).

What the user is told:
- iOS sets no message on success.
- Android toasts 'Imported %1$s' (MapScreen.kt:461-464).
- Both headers show the green 'Offline basemap' label for any PDFMapSource/PdfMapSource (ContentView.swift:578-594; MapScreen.kt:227-236).
- The iOS Layers label shows 'Manually placed bounds' because kind is .calibratedPDF when fromGeoPDF is false. The 'No georeferencing' branch needs bounds == nil, which never happens after import or restore (LayersSheet.swift:177-181).
- Neither platform has an unregistered or not-georeferenced state anywhere (grep found none).

I rate this high rather than critical. For a plain PDF, calibration is the intended workflow and a Calibrate button exists. The misregistration becomes critical through D5-01, which is already counted. The missing warning is still a real hazard for a field user.

iOS:
- ActiveMapSelectionStore.save sets state.retained = selection for every non-online source (ActiveMapSelectionStore.swift:131-136).
- executeMapSelectionTransition then calls reconcileManagedMapFiles on success (MapViewModel.swift:372-375).
- reconcile keeps only the retained URL (:234-270). ManagedImportedMapFileLifecycle.reconcile then removes every other managed candidate in ImportedMaps and offline_tiles (PDFSessionStore.swift:553-575).

Android:
- saveActiveAndRetainedPdf/Offline overwrite retainedImported (ActiveMapSelectionStore.kt:198-213).
- On success, reconcile deletes everything under pdf_maps, mbtiles and offline_tiles except `keep` (:274-313; MapViewModel.kt:455-456).

Neither import flow shows a confirmation. A grep for replace or remove warnings found nothing. The data loss is real. Originals usually still exist in Files or Downloads, and manual calibrations survive by content hash, so this is high rather than critical.

- The Android LayersSheet 'Unload PDF Map' and 'Unload Offline Tiles' buttons call their callbacks directly (LayersSheet.kt:189-199). MapScreen.kt:2041-2049 wires these straight to vm.unloadPdfMap() and vm.unloadOfflineTiles() with no dialog.
- Both functions pass clearRetained = (retained is that type) (MapViewModel.kt:234-258). ActiveMapSelectionCommitCoordinator.unloadImportedMap then calls saveOnlineAndClearRetained (:109-117).
- The subsequent reconcile takes the ONLINE/null branch with keep = emptySet() and deletes all managed files (ActiveMapSelectionStore.kt:296-312).
- iOS puts the same action behind a destructive confirmation alert (LayersSheet.swift:112-118) and offers a separate non-destructive 'Switch to Online Basemap'.

There is one small mitigation on Android: the sheet text says to choose an online basemap above to switch away without removing the map. The 'Unload' label and the lack of confirmation still make one-tap loss of a large MBTiles pack plausible.

Deletion after a bake:
- On iOS, a successful bake calls mapVM.selectMapSource(OfflineTileMapSource) (LayersSheet.swift:154-156). Reconcile then takes the retained-offlineTiles branch, calls PDFSessionStore.clear() and keeps only the .mbtiles (ActiveMapSelectionStore.swift:247-253). The PDF in ImportedMaps is unlinked.
- On Android, vm.setMapSource(offline) runs activateOffline, which calls saveActiveAndRetainedOffline. Reconcile's OFFLINE_TILES branch clears the PDF session and keeps only that file (ActiveMapSelectionStore.kt:288-295).
- The UI text does not warn about any of this.

Android zoom: PdfTiler.zoomRange uses pxPerDeg = pageWidth(pt)/lonSpan and floor(log2(pxPerDeg*360/256)) (PdfTiler.kt:223-226). My script (fitting the USGS correspondences, taking page corners 0..1728 x 0..2088, lonSpan 0.1662) gives log2 = 13.84, so maxZoom is 13. That is 15.1 m/px at 37.8N, against 8.47 m/px for 1:24k at 72 dpi. The tile budget does not bind: z11-13 is only 38 tiles.

iOS zoom: it accumulates to 2,500 tiles over the 1.2x-padded coverage and reaches z16 (1.89 m/px, about 2,300 tiles total). The claimed divergence holds.

iOS:
- tilingTask is a Task.detached stored in LayersSheet @State (LayersSheet.swift:18-20, 146). Nothing cancels it: there is no onDisappear or interactiveDismissDisabled in the file.
- Progress and Cancel live only in the sheet (:197-210). Sheet @State resets when the sheet is presented again, so 'Generate Offline Tiles…' reappears.
- On completion, MainActor.run calls mapVM.selectMapSource(source), which switches to A's tiles. Through D5-05's reconcile that deletes any PDF imported in the meantime.
- There is no beginBackgroundTask anywhere in ios/.
- An uncalibrated fallback PDF has placementTransform == nil (PDFMapSource.swift:42-45), so PDFTiler.generate returns nil at :18-22. The user then sees 'Check that the device has free storage' (Messages.swift:880).

Android:
- The bake dialog has onDismissRequest as a no-op and an empty confirmButton, so there is no Cancel (MapScreen.kt:1950-1969).
- Every null result from PdfTiler, including disk-full and render errors, which are caught as Throwable and turned into null (PdfTiler.kt:125-130), shows 'calibrate the PDF first' (MapScreen.kt:2030-2034).
- renderFirstPageStrips opens a new descriptor and PdfRenderer on every tile (PdfPageRenderer.kt:163-172).

'Minutes' is overstated for the USGS sheet, which is only about 49 tiles at the z13 cap, but it holds for budget-sized bakes.

The structure is exactly as described:
- iOS preparePDF only constructs the PDFDocument and page 0 and reads mediaBox. It never draws (ContentView.swift:412-421).
- selectMapSource persists the session and selector before publication.
- onAppear then calls restoreActiveBasemap (ContentView.swift:945), and updateUIView calls syncPDF, which calls pdf.renderedImage() synchronously on main (TileMapContainer.swift:113, 377-379).
- Android persists the picker result to prefs (MainActivity.kt:489-497) and replays it from a LaunchedEffect. After process death it runs again because only a terminal result clears it (MapScreen.kt:595-613).
- PdfGroundLayer renders the restored source on every launch (CustomMapOverlays.kt:822-829).
- A grep for crash-loop, safe-mode or render-marker logic found nothing.

I down-rate this to medium because the trigger (a render that kills the process) is not demonstrated. Output bitmaps are capped at 4096 px / 32 MB. pdfium streams DCT images, and I believe it uses try-alloc for OpenJPEG. So the '600 dpi A0 scan' scenario may just fail to render rather than abort.

To settle it at runtime: import a large JPX-compressed scan, and a known-crashing fuzzed PDF, on a low-RAM Android device and on an older iPhone. Watch for a SIGABRT or jetsam event during the first render and on relaunch. If a crash does occur, the loop is certain and the impact is severe.

iOS rendering: syncPDF calls pdf.renderedImage() inside updateUIView on main (TileMapContainer.swift:102-113, 377-379). PDFMapSource's own comment says this call is heavy and off-main only (PDFMapSource.swift:86-88).

iOS hashing:
- PDFSessionStore.load hashes in resolveImportedMap (PDFSessionStore.swift:293) and again at :177.
- load is reached from reconcile through source(for: retained) (ActiveMapSelectionStore.swift:243, 407), from restoreRetained, and from restoreActive.
- reconcile runs after every successful selection, including online style switches (MapViewModel.swift:372-375), and after restoreRetainedMapSelection (:275-279).
- Opening Layers with an online source while a PDF is retained runs refreshRetainedMap (restoreRetained = 2 hashes, plus reconcile = 2). Tapping a style adds reconcile (2), then another refresh (4). That is roughly 10 SHA-256 passes on main. Note that if the PDF itself is active, refreshRetainedMap returns early (LayersSheet.swift:322-327), so the cost applies to the retained-but-inactive case.

Android: PdfSessionStore.save hashes the file for any Calibration.Fiduciaries (PdfSessionStore.kt:94-98). Auto-parsed GeoPDFs become Fiduciaries through base.calibrated (MapScreenHelpers.kt:498). vm.setMapSource runs on Main after withContext(IO) returns (MapScreen.kt:461-462).

iOS: importWorkTask (ContentView.swift:517) is only assigned or cancelled and is never bound to any UI. A grep for importing or progress state found nothing on either platform.

Android: IdempotentDocumentCopy calls validate = preflightPdfImport, which is PdfRenderer.firstPageInfo plus a PDDocument.load in pageRotation (MapScreenHelpers.kt:462-465, 424-439). Then there is a second preflightPdfImport(dest) (:469), then GeoPdfParser.parse, which is a third PDDocument.load (:495; GeoPdfParser.kt:66). That makes 3 PDFBox loads and 2 PdfRenderer opens per import.

The copy loop (DocumentImportCopy.kt:154-164) is blocking and has no cancellation check. receiveDocumentImportResult releases the previous grant before publishing the new pending import (MainActivity.kt:417-419). On iOS, handleImport cancels the prior importWorkTask silently (ContentView.swift:1954).

Android:
- LaunchedEffect(mapSource.id) resets calibration state only when the new source is not a PdfMapSource (MapScreen.kt:709-715).
- The Menu button and Import/Export stay visible during calibration (:1139, :1219-1226). Only the bottom bar changes (:1404).
- finishPdfCalibration fits the retained calibrationFiduciaries (A's page points and MGRS) and applies them to the current pdfSource, which is B (:850-856).
- setMapSource then calls PdfSessionStore.save, which calls saveToLibrary under B's content hash (PdfSessionStore.kt:94-98). Because the MGRS strings are non-blank, the entry is treated as manual and wins on re-import (MapScreenHelpers.kt:485-487).

iOS: CalibrationSession.source is weak (CalibrationSession.swift:35). Nothing cancels the calibration when the source changes; the only cancel() calls are at ContentView.swift:1237, 1556 and 1936. Taps keep recording (MapEditingController.swift:145-151). When A is released, finishCalibration's guard on calibration.source returns silently (ContentView.swift:1919-1921).

I down-rate to medium:
- It needs an unusual sequence: start calibrating, import another PDF, then tap Finish while A's markers are visibly misplaced on B.
- The bad library entry is not permanent. Recalibrating B overwrites it.

iOS:
- CalibrationSession.finish catches the fit error with a print and returns nil (CalibrationSession.swift:94-104). finishCalibration then returns silently (ContentView.swift:1919-1921).
- If applyCalibration rejects the fit (off-Earth corner or non-invertible, PDFMapSource.swift:109-138), newSource keeps bounds == nil because it was built with bounds: nil at ContentView.swift:1925. PDFSessionStore.save returns false at :78-81. The activate transition then reports .pdfSession, which shows 'could not be saved for relaunch', and Retry replays the same failing transition.
- lastFitRMSMetres is set in finish() and then cleared by calibration.cancel() on success (ContentView.swift:1936; CalibrationSession.swift:52). The 'Previous fit RMS' row (CalibrationOverlay.swift:40-45) therefore only ever appears after a failed selection.

Android:
- calibrated() returns `this` on validation failure (PdfMapSource.kt:22-27). setMapSource(this) succeeds and the RMS toast is shown (MapScreen.kt:856-859).
- isCalibratingPdf is cleared. The next startPdfCalibration seeds from source.calibration, which is null for a fallback source, so the typed points are lost.

With 3 points the affine is exactly determined, so the RMS is 0 whatever typos the points contain.

Android: preflightPdfImport rejects rotation != 0, and it rejects a null result from pageRotation (PDFBox could not load the file) with the 'Flatten or print it' message (MapScreenHelpers.kt:432-438; GeoPdfParser.kt:101-111).

iOS:
- There is no rotation handling. PDFRasteriser sizes the canvas from page.bounds(for: .mediaBox) or the crop, then calls page.draw(with: .mediaBox, to:) (PDFOverlay.swift:106-140). PDFTiler does the same (PDFTiler.swift:204-210).
- The only test asserts a non-empty raster (PDFImportSmokeTests.swift:115-134).
- The divergence between platforms is certain.

The exact iOS visual result needs a runtime check. As far as I know, PDFPage.draw(with:to:) applies the page's /Rotate while bounds(for:) does not, so a 90/270 page would render rotated and clipped into a canvas with the unrotated aspect. To settle it: render a /Rotate 90 fixture with a marker square and inspect the pixel positions.

Every path hard-codes page 0:
- iOS GeoPDFReader page(at: 0) (:159-161).
- iOS PDFRasteriser (PDFOverlay.swift:106-107) and PDFTiler (:18-22).
- iOS import validation (PDFMapImporter.swift:24-27; ContentView.swift:414-416).
- Android GeoPdfParser doc.getPage(0) (:66-67).
- Android PdfPageRenderer openPage(0) (:68-75 and every render).

The catalog /VP is consulted only when page 0 has no /VP (iOS :163-166; Android :69-74). pageCount is used only for a '> 0' check, and nothing notices or prompts when a file has several pages. A GeoPDF whose map is on page 2 therefore gets the silent fallback from D5-02.

iOS:
- uniqueDestination keeps the source stem as the file name (ContentView.swift:102-122).
- Files go to Application Support/ImportedMaps (:125-131). Baked tiles go to Application Support/offline_tiles (PDFTiler.swift:42-46).
- A grep of all of ios/ finds no isExcludedFromBackup, so both locations are in iCloud and Finder backups by default.

Android: allowBackup=false, fullBackupContent=false, and data_extraction_rules exclude all domains for both cloud backup and device transfer (AndroidManifest.xml:28-30). Copies use opaque import-<sha>.pdf names (DocumentImportCopy.kt:95-100).

THREAT_MODEL.md:415-421 acknowledges that the map files are plaintext at rest but only discusses filesystem extraction. It says nothing about backup upload for these files.

- GeoPdfParser.parse and pageRotation both call PDDocument.load(file) with default settings inside Kotlin runCatching, which catches Throwable, including OutOfMemoryError and StackOverflowError (GeoPdfParser.kt:61-93, 101-111).
- There is no MemoryUsageSetting anywhere in the main sources, and the library is pdfbox-android 2.0.27.0 (build.gradle.kts:411).
- The file is loaded 3 times per import (see D5-09).
- An OOM inside pageRotation turns into null, which shows the misleading 'could not safely inspect page rotation' message.
- pdfium runs in-process through PdfRenderer.
- The THREAT_MODEL §3 trust table (lines 47-56) lists symbol packs as untrusted but not imported PDFs or MBTiles.

The impact is mainly denial of service from a crafted file. Combined with the Android pending-import replay (D5-07), a process kill during import could repeat on every launch. Medium is fair; it is not higher.

Android: PdfGroundLayer catches Exception and does nothing, and `val image = bmp ?: return` then draws nothing (CustomMapOverlays.kt:822-846). Meanwhile the header still reports 'Offline basemap' because it only checks the source type.

iOS: syncPDF's guard removes the overlay and mask when renderedImage() returns nil (TileMapContainer.swift:377-383). renderedImage caches only on success (PDFMapSource.swift:89-104). Each updateUIView therefore re-opens the PDFDocument and retries on main.

visibility.pdfOverlayVisible appears only in LayersSheet.swift:174 (the Toggle binding) and LayerVisibility.swift:16/46/64 (declaration and persistence). Nothing in Map/Renderer reads it. syncPDF (TileMapContainer.swift:377-405) always attaches the PDF image and mask.

persistPendingDocumentImport writes the URI string in plaintext to the 'pending_document_import_v1' SharedPreferences (MainActivity.kt:489-497, 699-702). audit.summary:
Data flow. iOS: ContentView import → PDFMapImporter.copyAndValidate → GeoPDFReader.bounds (Adobe /VP /Measure GPTS+LPTS fitted by AffineFitter into a PDF-user-space(y-up) → lon/lat AffineTransform2D; otherwise LGIDict CTM+Neatline via Projection/DatumShift with a 50 m RMS gate; otherwise a 10 km box centred on the camera) → PDFMapSource → PDFRasteriser (1 px per PDF point, max 4096 px) → PDFImageOverlayView, which projects the four crop corners through the affine and MapCamera (Web Mercator, points) → MGRSGridOverlayView (NGA mgrs-ios with vendored Snyder UTM). An optional PDFTiler bakes MBTiles in 0.25° strips. Android: importPdfMapSource → preflight (rejects /Rotate) → GeoPdfParser (PDFBox; Adobe, or LGIDict Registration/CTM via LgiProjection) → AffineFitter → PdfMapSource.calibrated → PdfGroundLayer (whole-page bitmap, setPolyToPoly, dp camera × density) plus MgrsGridCanvas (mgrs-java 2.1.3). PdfTiler uses PdfRenderer strips.

What is solid: the WebMercator, MapCamera and TileMath suites mirror each other (WebMercatorTests/MapCameraTests/TileMathTests and RenderMathTest). Other well-covered areas: AffineFitter hardening on both platforms, the MBTiles store (iOS), raster sizing, fail-closed handling of malformed LGIDict/Adobe metadata (iOS unit tests, Android instrumented), LgiProjection UTM/TM against NGA, and DatumTests.

Gaps:
- **Untested on both:** any GeoPDF from a real producer (the USGS sample is never parsed), grid line and label geometry (only stroke widths are tested), pixel correctness of generated tiles, calibration tap→PDF mapping, zoom-range and grid-density policy, and on-device alignment.
- **iOS only:** PDFTiler and WebMercatorTiles have no tests at all.
- **Android only:** GeoPDF parsing is covered only by instrumented tests; PdfGroundLayer and pdfPointFor are untested.
- **Shared fixtures:** just 2 exact affine cases and 4 MGRS points, with a 1e-3° round-trip tolerance.

As a result, both critical bugs pass every suite: the USGS sample is rejected on both platforms, and every northern-hemisphere northing grid label reads 1 km low.

All evidence scripts and the executable verification harness are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cbrooker-Code-TacticalMaps/d9f42208-9d3f-40e1-9b8b-49fa6c488260/scratchpad/audit/ (called "audit/" below):
- gen_grid_pdfs.py and tm.py: 12 synthetic UTM-gridded PDFs in out/, each checked with poppler (59 of 59 non-corner intersections land on printed ink).
- out/pdf_grid_sheets(.trimmed).json and out/usgs_sf_north_expected.json.
- grid_alignment.py: screenshot analyser with a self-test.
- Replicas: sim_usgs_vp.py, ios_labels.py/snyder.py, GridLabels.java and GridCost.java (run against the real NGA jar), tiler_rotation.py, zoomrange.py, android_tap.py, usgs_affine_err.py, sim_overlay.py.

findings.title: Real USGS/Esri GeoPDFs are rejected on both platforms (LPTS slightly outside [0,1]); no test parses a GeoPDF from a real producer
findings.description: The /VP of samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf (page obj 20, Esri ArcSOC 10.8.1) has a 'Map Layers' viewport with BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373] and Measure obj 424 with LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514] (/Bounds is identical). Esri writes the control quad slightly outside the unit square. Both parsers require every LPTS value to be in [0,1], so the map body is classed as malformed. Its area (3,510,016 pt²) is larger than the two valid insets (Quadrangle Location 5,006 pt², Adjoining Sheet 3,336 pt²), so the whole Adobe path returns Rejected/.rejected and no georeference is produced. Commit 1c023de (2026-09-17) introduced this. Existing tests lock the behaviour in: the LPTS-1.1 case and the 'larger malformed map body must reject' cases. ScreenshotTests imports this exact file but only waits for the 'Map' button, with device location already set to the sheet centre. The fallback centred on the camera therefore looks plausible and hides the regression.
findings.failure_scenario: Import any Esri-produced US Topo (2016+) such as USGS_SF_North.pdf. iOS: GeoPDFReader.bounds returns nil, so a 10 km fallbackBounds square is centred on the camera, stretched, with kind .calibratedPDF, and the Layers sheet says 'Manually placed bounds'. Android: GeoPdfParser.parse returns null, so importPdfMapSource returns the uncalibrated 10 km box. The sheet is misregistered by the camera distance (km to thousands of km), and the MGRS grid and GPS dot do not match. The Python replica audit/sim_usgs_vp.py prints 'RESULT: REJECTED (no georef)'. The synthetic audit/out/tacmap_grid_sf_esri.pdf reproduces the same LPTS shape.
findings.suggested_fix: In both parsers, accept LPTS within a tolerance (for example -0.05..1.05) and gate instead on fit quality: AffineFitter RMS at or below about one PDF point in ground metres, and crossValidated. Keep 1.1 rejected. Add the USGS arrays as a regression fixture. Make the screenshot/UI test assert georeferenced status (kind == .geoPDF, or the 'Georeferenced' Layers text) instead of only the Map button.
findings.proving_test: iOS PDFImportSmokeTests.testEsriUSTopoViewportWithQuadJustOutsideUnitSquareIsAccepted: parametrise makeRawPDF's MediaBox to [0 0 1728 2088] and use pageExtras '/VP [<< /BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373] /Measure << /Subtype /GEO /GPTS [37.73318 -122.52121 37.88898 -122.52021 37.88818 -122.35264 37.73238 -122.354] /LPTS [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514] >> >> <<small valid inset>>]'. Assert GeoPDFReader.bounds(from:)?.placementAffine is non-nil, and that apply(CGPoint(x:0,y:2098.44)) is within 10 m of 37.88898,-122.52021. It currently fails. Add testRealUSGSSample, guarded by XCTSkipUnless(samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf exists), checking out/usgs_sf_north_expected.json printedGridIntersections within 10 m.
