findings.title: MGRS grid northing labels read one unit low across the northern hemisphere on both platforms; grid geometry and labels have zero tests
findings.description: Each label is MGRS.from(average of the segment's two lat/lon endpoints), followed by integer truncation: (v/1000)%100 for 1 km and (v/10000)%10 for 10 km. A constant-northing UTM line bows in lat/lon, so the chord midpoint lies south of the line: 0.0197 m for a 1 km segment and 1.52 m for a 10 km segment (checked with an independent Krüger TM, audit/tm.py). NGA rounds the northing to the centimetre (…999.98) and MGRS.from truncates it (MGRS.swift:413), giving the previous kilometre. Easting lines fail the same way wherever the bow points west, for example 10 km easting labels in the southern hemisphere west of the central meridian (CM). The only grid tests on either platform check stroke widths.
findings.failure_scenario: Grid on at zoom 12 or more over San Francisco: the line printed as northing '81' (N=4181000) is labelled '80', and every northing label in view is 1 km low. The 10 km line N=4170000 is labelled '6' instead of '7'. Evidence: audit/GridLabels.java, run against the real mil.nga mgrs-2.1.3.jar with Android's exact logic, finds 483 of 966 KILOMETER labels wrong (all horizontal), 104,414 of 206,738 wrong over 47–50°N, and 1,574 of 2,520 wrong for TEN_KILOMETER. audit/ios_labels.py, replicating the vendored Snyder UTM with its rounding, finds 500 of 1000 wrong at SF, 400 of 800 at 50°N, and 100 of 200 10 km easting labels wrong at Sydney. A field user reading a grid reference off the overlay reports a northing that is 1000 m wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Label each line from the value it was generated from. Use UTM.from(line.point1, zone.number, zone.hemisphere), or the NGA line's UTM easting/northing, rounded to the nearest grid precision rather than a truncated midpoint MGRS. Pin the rule in a shared fixture.
findings.proving_test: iOS MGRSGridRendererTests.testEveryLabelEqualsItsLineValue: MGRSGridRenderer.build(for: MKCoordinateRegion(center 37.78,-122.43, span 0.06x0.07), mapWidthPoints: 400). For each .KILOMETER label, round UTM.from(label.coordinate)'s easting (vertical) or northing (horizontal) to 1000 and assert String(format:"%02d") == label.text. About 50% fail today. Android JVM MgrsGridRendererLabelTest does the same with MgrsGridRenderer.build(37.75,-122.47,37.81,-122.40,1000) and MGRS.from(Point.point(lng,lat)).toUTM(). Share testdata/mgrs_grid_labels.json with regions 10N east and west of CM, 56S, and the 33N zone edge, listing each line's axis, value and expected 1 km and 10 km labels (generator: audit/gen_grid_pdfs.py gridLines).

findings.title: Android re-calibration maps taps through the coverage bbox, not the affine the page is drawn with; neither platform tests calibration tap mapping
findings.description: When the source already has a calibration (an auto-parsed GeoPDF, or an earlier manual fit), startPdfCalibration keeps it. PdfGroundLayer then draws the page through that affine, including rotation and shear. However, onCalibrationTap → PdfMapSource.pdfPointFor interpolates the tap's lat/lon linearly across source.coverage, which is the axis-aligned bbox of the affine-projected page corners (calibratedPdfBounds). iOS converts the tap through the transformed UIImageView (convert(_:from:)), which is correct. No test covers either mapping, and neither platform has an automated calibration-flow test.
findings.failure_scenario: Import tacmap_grid_sf_iso.pdf, which auto-georeferences, then open Calibrate and tap exactly on fiducial F1. The stored PDF point is off by up to 3.7 pt (33 m). On the zone-edge sheet (about 2° convergence) the error is 23.5 pt (207 m). A scan calibrated once at 5° rotation and then refined with a 4th point gets 53 pt (468 m), and the refit drags the whole map. Replica: audit/android_tap.py.
findings.suggested_fix: When a calibration exists, map taps with calibration.transform.inverted().apply(lon, lat). Keep the bbox interpolation only for the uncalibrated stretched display, or switch the display back to uncalibrated when calibration starts.
findings.proving_test: Extract a pure internal fun pdfPointForTap(transform: AffineTransform2D?, coverage: Wgs84Bounds, pageInfo: PdfPageInfo, lat, lon), since PdfMapSource needs android.net.Uri, which JVM tests cannot use. JVM test PdfCalibrationTapMappingTest: take a 5°-rotated transform (from the audit/out/pdf_grid_sheets.json rot5_iso fiducials) and assert pdfPointForTap(transform.apply(P)) == P within 0.5 pt for each fiducial. Today the error is up to 53 pt. Also add an iOS unit test for PDFImageOverlayView.pdfPoint(forScreenTap:inView:) after a rotated updateFrame, so the correct behaviour stays pinned.

findings.title: Offline tile bake drops the affine's rotation and shear on both platforms; iOS PDFTiler has no tests and Android's only counts tiles
findings.description: Each strip maps the axis-aligned bbox of the inverse-affine image of its lon/lat box onto the tile band using scale and translate only (ctx.scaleBy/translateBy on iOS, Matrix.setRectToRect(FILL) on Android). Any rotation or shear in the calibration is thrown away: grid convergence, a skewed scan, or a non-rectangular GeoPDF control quad. Every tile re-anchors to its own bbox, so the error shows up as seams between tiles. The only tiler test on either platform checks that tile count equals the progress total, using an axis-aligned transform. iOS WebMercatorTiles is also untested; only Android's WebMercatorTilesTest.kt exists.
findings.failure_scenario: A scan calibrated at 5° rotation, then 'Generate offline tiles': content lands up to 22.4 px from its true position inside every z12–z16 tile, with jogs of similar size at the seams. A 2° zone-edge GeoPDF gives 9 px; USGS SF (0.34°) gives 1.5 px. The printed grid zig-zags against the MGRS overlay after baking. Replica: audit/tiler_rotation.py simulates the shared strip algorithm.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw each tile, or each strip, with the full affine. Concatenate the inverse calibration (lon/lat→page) with the strip's lon/lat→pixel mapping into one CGAffineTransform (iOS) or android.graphics.Matrix.setPolyToPoly with 3–4 point pairs (Android), instead of fitting a bbox to a rect.
findings.proving_test: iOS PDFTilerTests.testRotatedCalibrationKeepsPrintedGridOnFixturePixels: load testdata/pdf/tacmap_grid_rot5_plain.pdf and applyCalibration with the fixture's 4 fiducials (MGRS→lat/lon), then run PDFTiler.generate. For each gridIntersection's tiles['16'], read MBTilesStore.tile(z:x:y:), decode it with UIImage(data:), and assert a red pixel (R>180, G<90, B<90) within 1.5 px of px. Android instrumented twin: PdfTiler.generate(context, source) → SQLiteDatabase → BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray → the same check. Add iOS WebMercatorTilesTests mirroring WebMercatorTilesTest.kt.

findings.title: Android offline tiles stop at the page's 72-dpi resolution (z13 for USGS) and the camera is clamped there; live overlays on both platforms are rasterised at 1 px per PDF point
findings.description: Android sets maxZoom = floor(log2(pageWidthPts/lonSpan*360/256)), which is the page's native 72-dpi resolution. iOS limits only by budget (2,500 tiles). Once the MBTiles source is active, both renderers clamp pinch zoom to the source's min and max. Before baking, the live PDF overlays come from one raster at scale min(1,…), i.e. 1 px per PDF point, which is 8.47 m/px on a 1:24k sheet. The existing tests assert exactly this 'no upscale' behaviour, and no test relates ground resolution to camera zoom or checks parity of the tiler's zoom range.
findings.failure_scenario: Georeferenced USGS SF North → 'Generate offline tiles'. Android bakes z11–z13 (15.1 m/px), and the user can no longer zoom in past z13 or out past z11. iOS bakes z10–z16 (1.9 m/px). The live overlay before baking is 8.5 m/px on both platforms, so at z17 each PDF pixel covers about 9 pt of screen and 6 pt map text is unreadable. Replica: audit/zoomrange.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive max zoom from map scale (for example at least 3 px per PDF point, capped by budget) with the same pure function on both platforms, pinned by a fixture. Allow overzoom past source.maxZoom. Render the live overlay per visible tile from vectors, or at 3 px/pt or more within a memory budget.
findings.proving_test: Make zoomRange internal on both platforms and add testdata/tiler_zoom_ranges.json (page 1728x2088, coverage from usgs_sf_north_expected.json, expected minZoom/maxZoom). The Android JVM PdfTilerZoomRangeTest asserts maxZoom >= 16 and fails today with 13; iOS PDFTilerZoomRangeTests asserts the same values. UI: after baking, pinch out 6 times and assert the scale bar reads 50 m or less.

findings.title: Android chooses MGRS grid density from device pixels instead of dp (1 km grid about 1.4 zoom levels too early) and rebuilds the grid on every camera frame
findings.description: MgrsGridCanvas passes coverageWidthPx = hypot(dp viewport) * density into build(). build()'s zoom heuristic assumes 256-unit tiles in the camera's unit, which is dp, so the effective grid zoom is camera zoom + log2(density) (+1.39 at 2.625x). iOS passes points. The remember keys include centerLat and centerLon, so every pan frame rebuilds the grid; iOS uses a 0.001° fingerprint instead. Neither platform tests the density thresholds.
findings.failure_scenario: On a Pixel-7-class device (411x914 dp, 2.625x) at camera z10.2 over SF, Android draws the 1 km grid at 9.5 dp spacing: 22,960 segments, each with a label computed via MGRS.from. It rebuilds all of it on every pan frame, taking 33 ms on a desktop JVM and several times that on a phone. The result is a grey mesh and jank. iOS at the same camera zoom shows only the 100 km and 10 km lines. Replica: audit/GridCost.java against the NGA jar.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the dp width (coverageWidthPx / density), or subtract log2(density). Key the rebuild on a coarse fingerprint like iOS, and cap the segment and label count.
findings.proving_test: Android JVM MgrsGridDensityTest: compute mapWidthPx exactly as CustomMapOverlays does for camera z10.2, 411x914 dp at density 2.625. Assert MgrsGridRenderer.build returns no KILOMETER lines and fewer than 3,000 segments; today it returns 22,960. Add a shared testdata/grid_density.json (camera zoom, viewport, density → expected grid types) and assert the same types on iOS via MGRSGridRenderer.build(for:mapWidthPoints:).

findings.title: The datum declared in an ISO/Adobe GeoPDF's /GCS is ignored on both platforms (only PRIMEM is read); untested
findings.description: GPTS are expressed in the geographic CRS of /GCS: either a GEOGCS, or the GEOGCS inside a PROJCS. Both parsers read only PRIMEM and treat GPTS as WGS84. The LGIDict path applies a datum shift; the Adobe path does not. No test has a non-WGS84 GCS.
findings.failure_scenario: Import an Adobe GeoPDF whose /GCS WKT is GEOGCS["NAD27",…Clarke 1866…], such as older or historical USGS quads, at San Francisco. The NAD27 corner coordinates are used as WGS84, so the sheet is misregistered by about 93 m (11 m N, 92.5 m E; audit Molodensky check). ED50 sheets are off by 100 m or more, and Tokyo-datum sheets by about 450 m. The printed grid sits that far from the MGRS overlay and the GPS dot.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse DATUM/SPHEROID (and TOWGS84 or a known EPSG code) from the GCS WKT or /EPSG and shift with DatumShift (iOS) or LgiDatum (Android). Fail closed on unknown datums other than WGS84, NAD83, GDA or ETRS.
findings.proving_test: Generate a variant of audit/out/tacmap_grid_sf_iso.pdf with a NAD27 GEOGCS WKT and GPTS converted to NAD27 (Molodensky dx -8, dy 160, dz 176). Parse with iOS GeoPDFReader.bounds and Android GeoPdfParser.parse, then assert either rejection or placement of every fixture gridIntersection within 5 m of its WGS84 truth. Today the placement is about 93 m off.

findings.title: The Adobe path fits a page→lat/lon affine to 4 GPTS, leaving a 4–8 m mismatch between printed grid and overlay on the USGS quad; no alignment tolerance is tested
findings.description: The USGS page is a linear image of UTM 10N: the page→UTM affine has only 0.22 m residual at its four controls, and /GCS is a PROJCS. The app instead fits lon/lat directly (4 points, 6 parameters), which gives 7.9 m RMS at the controls and 4–6 m at interior printed 1000 m intersections. The LGIDict path accepts up to 50 m RMS. The Adobe path has no gate on either platform. No test compares placement against the printed-grid truth.
findings.failure_scenario: Once D6-01 is fixed, view USGS SF at z18 (0.47 m/pt): the overlay line sits up to about 13 pt from the printed line, so the user sees two grids. The smaller 6–8 km synthetic sheets show 1.5 m (sf) and 2.9 m (zone edge). Replicas: audit/usgs_affine_err.py and audit/sim_overlay.py (the screenshot analyser reproduces 1.5 m and 3.0 m).
findings.suggested_fix: When the CRS is projected (PROJCS or a projected LGIDict), keep the page→projected affine and convert through the projection per vertex or strip in the overlay and tiler. Alternatively, fit on a dense sample and apply per-tile correction. Tighten the RMS gates.
findings.proving_test: Shared fixture test on both platforms. For each printedGridIntersection in testdata/usgs_sf_north_expected.json and pdf_grid_sheets.json, apply placementAffine to pdf on iOS, or AffineFitter.fit(correspondences).transform.apply on Android. Assert the distance to lat/lon truth is within tolerances.targetMaxMetres = 1 m, with an interim 10 m guard. Add an on-device check: audit/grid_alignment.py on a z18 screenshot must report at most 1.5 px.

findings.title: iOS ignores LGIDict /Registration (requires /CTM) while Android supports it; the divergence is untested on iOS
findings.description: Android uses LGIDict /Registration point pairs first and falls back to /CTM. iOS reads only /CTM with /Neatline and returns crop-only when /CTM is missing. Android's instrumented tests use Registration fixtures (including projected UTM); iOS tests use only CTM.
findings.failure_scenario: A TerraGo-style LGIDict with /Registration and no /CTM (audit/out/tacmap_grid_sf_lgireg.pdf) is georeferenced on Android. On iOS, GeoPDFReader.bounds returns nil, the camera-centred fallback is used, and the sheet is misregistered on iOS only.
findings.suggested_fix: Port registrationCorrespondences (projected CRS and datum handling included) into GeoPDFReader.parseLGIDictRaw, keeping the RMS gate.
findings.proving_test: iOS PDFImportSmokeTests.testLGIDictRegistrationOnlyProducesUTMPlacement uses pageExtras '/LGIDict << /Description (Layers) /Registration [[0 0 334000 6250000] [600 0 340000 6250000] [600 400 340000 6254000] [0 400 334000 6254000]] /Projection << /ProjectionType /UT /Zone 56 /Hemisphere /S /Datum /WE >> >>'. Assert placementAffine is non-nil and the corners match Projection.utm(zone:56,.SOUTH).inverse within 1e-4°. This mirrors Android's projectedLgiRegistrationUtmProducesRealWgs84ControlPoints.

findings.title: /Rotate and non-zero MediaBox/CropBox origins are handled differently on each platform; no registration test covers either
findings.description:
**Rotation.** Android rejects /Rotate≠0, while iOS imports rotated pages. The iOS test only checks that raster width and height are greater than 0, never placement.

**Box origin.** Android's GeoPDF correspondences are in raw PDF user space. PdfRenderer's page size and render matrix, however, are relative to the page box. PdfTiler (h - y flip) and PdfGroundLayer (corners at 0..pw, 0..ph) assume the box origin is (0,0). iOS uses rects that account for the mediaBox origin. No fixture has a non-zero origin or a rotated GeoPDF.
findings.failure_scenario:
**Origin.** A GeoPDF cropped in Acrobat or Preview (CropBox inset), or a producer MediaBox at [100 150 …] (audit/out/tacmap_grid_offset_iso.pdf). Treating raw user space as box-relative puts 0 of 63 grid intersections on the printed lines (poppler check), shifting the map by origin × scale: about 180 m for a 20 pt inset and about 1.3 km for a 150 pt origin at 1:25k. This is the likely Android behaviour.

**Rotation.** A /Rotate 90 GeoPDF is refused on Android, and its registration on iOS is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise page coordinates to one box on both platforms, in the parsers and in calibration taps: subtract the CropBox origin and apply /Rotate. Decide on one rotation policy for both platforms.
findings.proving_test: Use fixtures audit/out/tacmap_grid_offset_iso.pdf and a /Rotate 90 variant of sf_iso. iOS: GeoPDFReader.bounds, then PDFTiler.generate and PDFRasteriser.render, with pixel checks at the fixture's tile px (red within 1.5 px). Android instrumented: GeoPdfParser.parse, then PdfTiler.generate, with the same tile pixel checks. For rotation, assert the documented policy (accept with correct placement, or reject) identically on both platforms.

findings.title: Shared cross-platform fixtures don't cover the PDF/grid pipeline: parity rests on 2 exact affine cases and 4 MGRS points at a 1e-3° (~111 m) tolerance
findings.description:
**Current coverage.** affine_fits.json has two noise-free cases on a 1000×800 page, with no y-flip, rotation, realistic magnitudes (e.g. 1728×2088) or noisy over-determined case. mgrs_samples.json has 4 coordinates with a round-trip tolerance of 1e-3°.

**No shared vectors for:**
- GeoPDF parse outputs.
- UTM/TM inverse. iOS Projection.swift and Android LgiProjection.kt are separate implementations, and the MGRS libraries differ too: iOS uses vendored Snyder, Android the upstream NGA formula. They measured 1.1–4.5 cm apart for identical inputs, enough to flip truncated 1 m readouts.
- WebMercatorTiles (untested on iOS).
- Tiler zoom range, grid lines and labels, and grid density.
- Overlay placement: iOS tests pdfAffineOverlayPlacement, but Android's PdfGroundLayer is untested.
findings.failure_scenario: Cross-platform drift ships silently. Examples: D6-05 (z13 vs z16), D6-06 (grid density), D6-09 (Registration), and crosshair MGRS readouts that differ by 1 m between iOS and Android for the same point (UTM results in audit/java_utm.txt compared by the snippet in the transcript).
findings.suggested_fix:
Add the following and extend both SharedVectors suites:
- testdata/pdf/tacmap_grid_*.pdf: 12 files, about 2 KB each, from audit/gen_grid_pdfs.py.
- testdata/pdf_grid_sheets.json: audit/out/pdf_grid_sheets.trimmed.json, 112 KB.
- testdata/usgs_sf_north_expected.json.

findings.title: No end-to-end, on-device verification of placement or grid alignment exists, and the only real-GeoPDF UI test hides failures; executable harness and live test matrix (plan)
findings.description:
Current state: the iOS UI test only opens and cancels the picker. ScreenshotTests imports USGS but asserts only that the 'Map' button exists. The Android UI test imports a blank 200x300 page with no georeference. Nothing measures alignment.

Plan, with artifacts in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cbrooker-Code-TacticalMaps/d9f42208-9d3f-40e1-9b8b-49fa6c488260/scratchpad/audit/:

**(1) Generator: gen_grid_pdfs.py.** Stdlib plus tm.py (Krüger TM). reportlab, pypdf, pikepdf and fitz are not installed; only numpy, PIL and poppler are. It writes raw PDF 1.7 with Flate content in which the page is an exact linear image of UTM at 1:25,000 (8.819 m/pt):
- Pure-red 1000 m grid (1.4 pt on 10 km lines).
- 2-digit collar labels on all 4 sides.
- Corner ticks with full E/N.
- 4 black fiducial rings labelled with 10-digit MGRS.

Sheets: sf (10N 546–552 kmE / 4176–4184 kmN), edge (33N at 48.6°N, about 2° convergence), syd (56S), rot5 (frame rotated 5°), offset (MediaBox origin 100,150 with a 20 pt CropBox inset).

Metadata variants:
- iso: /VP /Measure /GEO GPTS/LPTS with /GCS PROJCS WKT.
- esri: the USGS quirk.
- lgictm: /CTM + /Neatline + /Projection UT /Datum WE.
- lgireg: /Registration only.
- plain: no geo metadata.

All 12 files parse in pdfinfo. verify_raster.py (poppler, 144 dpi) puts 59 of 59 non-corner predicted intersections on red ink.

**(2) Fixtures.** out/pdf_grid_sheets.json (a trimmed version exists) holds, per sheet: CRS, mediaBox, m/pt, page→UTM CTM, neatline, metadata arrays, fiducials (pdf, MGRS), gridIntersections (E, N, pdf, lat, lon, mgrs, and tile z/x/y plus pixel u,v at z14/16/18), gridLines (expected 1 km and 10 km labels) and tolerances. out/usgs_sf_north_expected.json holds the selected viewport, crop, controls, page→UTM affine, the 7.5' neatline on the page, and 9 printed intersections with truth, current-model error and tile px. Consumers are listed in D6-11.

**(3) Screenshot alignment: grid_alignment.py.**
- Classifies printed red, overlay grey (alpha 0.85) and their dark-red overlap.
- Finds lines with angle-searched projection profiles in 4 bands, so bends and rotation mismatches show up.
- Takes scale from the printed 1000 m spacing, so no zoom hook is needed.
- Reports px and metres per axis; the gate is worst ≤ max(1.5 px, 1 m).
- --selftest recovers an injected +3/−2 px offset within 0.5 px.
- On emulated app overlays (sim_overlay.py) it reproduces the analytic misfit: 1.5 m and 3.0 m against 1.5 m and 2.9 m.
- Capture with 'xcrun simctl io booted screenshot' or an XCUIScreen attachment on iOS, and 'adb exec-out screencap -p' on Android. Use --crop to exclude the HUD and --heading for rotated maps.

**(4) Live matrix (both platforms).** Grid on; location set with 'xcrun simctl location booted set 37.76,-122.45' or 'adb emu geo fix -122.45 37.76'.
- a) Import every synthetic file and USGS. Assert the georeferenced status: esri, lgireg and offset must georeference; plain must not. Fly to F1 via offline MGRS search and check the ring is within 2 px of screen centre.
- b) Take screenshots at z12, 14, 16 and 18 and run the analyser.
- c) Calibrate sf_plain and rot5_plain manually: tap the 4 rings, type the fixture MGRS, Finish, RMS ≤ 5 m, then run the analyser. Re-enter Calibrate and re-add F4 (catches D6-03).
- d) Zoom from min to max and back in 5 pinch steps each way. Check for no blank tiles, no 1 km lines below z12, and that the camera reaches at least z16 after Generate offline tiles (D6-05, D6-06).
- e) Pan across 256-px tile seams and the neatline edge after baking. Printed lines must stay continuous within 1 px (D6-04).
- f) Rotate the device (XCUIDevice.shared.orientation / UiDevice.setOrientationLeft) and rotate the map 30° (--heading 30).
- g) Switch basemap and then 'return to imported map'; the screenshot must match within 1 px.
- h) Kill and relaunch (app.terminate()+launch / 'adb shell am force-stop com.tacmap'). The same placement and fiducials must return, and the auto GeoPDF must be re-parsed.
- i) Delete or unload. The PDF and MBTiles must be gone ('xcrun simctl get_app_container booted com.tacticalmaps.app data'; 'adb shell run-as com.tacmap ls files/pdf_maps files/offline_tiles') and must not reappear after relaunch.
- j) Hostile inputs: /Rotate 90, password-protected, over 256 MB.

**File delivery.**
- iOS: file sharing is disabled, and 'simctl addmedia' accepts only photos, videos and contacts. Copy into Files local storage instead: G=$(xcrun simctl get_app_container booted com.apple.DocumentsApp groups | awk '$1=="group.com.apple.FileProvider.LocalStorage"{print $2}'); cp out/*.pdf "$G/File Provider Storage/". Then use Menu → Import / Export → PDF Map → Browse → On My iPhone; ScreenshotTests.importSeededGeoPDF can be reused. The 'copy into app Documents' instruction in samples/README is stale. Unit tests read testdata directly via #filePath.
- Android: 'adb push x.pdf /sdcard/Download/' plus 'adb shell content call --uri content://media --method scan_volume --arg external_primary'. Alternatively, write through MediaStore.Downloads inside the instrumentation as PdfImportSmokeTest.createPdfInDownloads does. Then pick in DocumentsUI (By.pkg("com.google.android.documentsui"), By.text(name)) and assert on the content description 'PDF map rendered: <name>', because uiautomator dumps are unreliable on Compose.

verdicts.reasoning:
I inflated the sample's object streams myself (verify/vp.py). Page /VP [0] 'Map Layers' has BBox [0 2088 1727.95998 56.69373] and Measure 424, whose LPTS and Bounds are both [-0.00708 1 0 -0.00514 1.00708 0 1 1.00514]. The two insets have LPTS [0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1]. The MediaBox is [0 0 1728 2088] with /Rotate 0.

**iOS.** GeoPDFReader.swift:347-350 requires (0.0...1.0).contains(normalX/normalY), so viewportAffine returns nil. :210-212 then records largestMalformedDeclaredGeoArea (about 3.51M pt²), which is larger than the best valid inset (about 5k pt²). :217-221 returns .rejected, :84-85 returns nil without trying LGIDict, and PDFMapImporter.swift:38-43 / ContentView.swift:1962 fall back to fallbackBounds with fromGeoPDF false, i.e. kind .calibratedPDF (PDFMapSource.swift:56).

**Android.** GeoPdfParser.kt:205-207 (`nx !in 0.0..1.0`) marks it malformed. :234-238 returns Rejected and :76-78 returns null, so MapScreenHelpers.kt:495 returns the uncalibrated base built on the camera-centred fallback (PdfMapSource.kt:43-56).

`git log -S` shows commit 1c023de introduced the range check and the malformed-area veto. The tests at PDFImportSmokeTests:195-220/339 and PdfImportHardeningInstrumentedTest:110-118 pin this behaviour with LPTS 1.1. ScreenshotTests:571 only waits for the 'Map' button. The flagship USGS US Topo import is misregistered on both platforms, so critical stands.

**Line generation.** Vendored GridZone.swift:150-186 (same in NGA Java) builds each segment as a single precision cell between UTM.point(E,N) and (E+p,N) or (E,N+p). MGRSGridRenderer.swift:100-105 and MgrsGridRenderer.kt:105-108 label each segment from MGRS.from of the lat/lon chord midpoint. Because a constant-northing curve is convex north in the northern hemisphere, that midpoint lies south of the line.

**Truncation.** MGRS.swift:413-414 truncates (Int(...)), and :130/:133 and kt:132/:136 truncate again. The label therefore drops to the previous km.

**Android check.** I ran the Android logic against the real mgrs-2.1.3 jar (verify/LabelVerify.java):
- SF 1 km: 49/49 horizontal labels wrong (line 4181000 labelled '80', mid northing 80999).
- SF 10 km: 48/48 wrong (4170000 labelled '6').
- 50°N: 192/192 wrong.
- Equator and Sydney horizontals: 0 wrong.
- Sydney 10 km verticals (west of CM 153): 143/143 wrong.

**iOS check.** I replicated the vendored Snyder, including the 1e-7° rounding at UTM.swift:148-149 and the cm rounding at :340/:347 (verify/ios_lbl.py). Results: SF 160/160 horizontal wrong, 50°N 400/400, Sydney 10 km verticals 100/100, equator about 0.

The labels are drawn verbatim (CustomMapOverlays.kt:327-329; TileMapContainer.swift:561-565). Every northing label on the grid overlay across the northern hemisphere reads 1 km (or 10 km) low, so critical is justified.

**The mismatch.** MapScreen.kt:845 keeps the existing fids when Calibrate starts, and the source stays calibrated. PdfGroundLayer (CustomMapOverlays.kt:845-866) warps the page through transform.apply of the 4 page corners with setPolyToPoly. But onCalibrationTap (MapScreen.kt:926-933) calls pdfPointFor (MapScreenHelpers.kt:65-80), which interpolates linearly across `coverage`. That coverage is the axis-aligned bbox of the affine corners (PdfMapSource.kt:76-105). Whenever the affine has rotation or shear, the tap-to-page mapping does not match what is drawn.

**Size of the error.** My replica (verify/tap.py, 700x900 pt page at 8.8 m/pt):
- 0.34° rotation: up to 4.2 pt (37 m).
- 2°: 24 pt (212 m).
- 5°: 57 pt (499 m).

These match the auditor's numbers. iOS converts through the transformed view (PDFOverlay.swift:288-299), which is correct.

Only re-calibration or refinement is affected; a first calibration on the stretched uncalibrated display is fine. That makes high the right rating rather than critical.

**iOS.** PDFTiler.swift:155-170 takes the bbox of the inverse-affine image of each strip, and :207-210 maps it to the band with scaleBy/translateBy only.

**Android.** PdfTiler.kt:187-219 does the same bbox step, and PdfPageRenderer.kt:183-184 maps with setRectToRect(FILL).

On both platforms any rotation or shear in the calibration is discarded and each tile re-anchors to its own bbox. My replica (unit-square tile, 256 px):
- 0.34°: 1.5 px max error.
- 2°: 8.6 px.
- 5°: 20.6 px.

This matches the auditor's 1.5/9/22.4. In ground terms the error is θ times the tile's ground size, so it is larger at low zoom (about 600 m at z12 for 5°).

The baked MBTiles becomes the active source (MapScreen.kt:2020-2028; LayersSheet.swift:147-156). There are no iOS PDFTiler or WebMercatorTiles tests (grep finds none). The Android instrumented test (:194-219) only counts tiles.

**Android zoom range.** PdfTiler.kt:223-226 sets maxZoom = floor(log2(pageWidth/lonSpan*360/256)). My replica (verify/d6/zr.py) fitted the USGS page from its real GPTS/LPTS: whole-page lon span 0.1662° with a 1728 pt width. That gives Android z11–z13 (15.1 m/px at max). iOS gets a budget-only range of z11–z16 (the auditor said z10; minor difference).

**Camera clamp.** After baking, the MBTiles source becomes active. Pinch zoom then clamps to source.minZoom/maxZoom on both platforms (TileMapView.kt:151-153, CustomMapScreen.kt:306-307, TileMapView.swift:162-164), so Android users cannot zoom past z13.

**Live overlays.** Both rasterise at scale min(1, …), i.e. at most 1 px per PDF point: PDFOverlay.swift:81-99 via PDFMapSource.swift:96, and PdfPageRenderer.kt:44-60/77-91. That is about 8.5 m/px on a 1:24k sheet and blurry at z16+.

No test ties resolution to zoom.

**Unit mismatch.** Android's MapCamera is in dp (MapProjection.kt:14-17 multiplies by density). CustomMapOverlays.kt:271-283 still passes mapWidthPx = hypot(dp)*density, and MgrsGridRenderer.kt:68-76 derives zoom assuming 256-unit tiles. The effective grid zoom is therefore camera zoom + log2(density).

**Measured with the real NGA jar** (verify/Density.java, 411x914 dp):
- z10.2 at density 2.625: zoomEst 12, KILOMETER lines, 23,198 segments, about 38 ms/build on desktop JVM, 9.5 dp spacing.
- Density 1.0 (the iOS points equivalent): zoomEst 10, 300 segments.
- On Android the 1 km grid appears from about z10.1; on iOS from z11.5.

**One overstatement.** The 'rebuilds every pan frame vs iOS fingerprint' contrast is weak. iOS's %.3f fingerprint (TileMapContainer.swift:553-558) changes about every 0.73 pt at z10, so iOS also rebuilds on almost every pan frame. The real divergence is the density-inflated segment count that Android rebuilds per frame (remember keys include centerLat/Lon/zoom).

iOS measurePrimeMeridian (GeoPDFReader.swift:391-416) and Android primeMeridianOffset (GeoPdfParser.kt:248-262) extract only PRIMEM from the /GCS WKT. viewportAffine (iOS :297-354) and the Android loop (:199-222) treat GPTS as WGS84 with no datum parse or shift.

The LGIDict paths do apply a datum: parseDatum on iOS and a converter on Android. A NAD27, ED50 or Tokyo Adobe GeoPDF (e.g. a USGS Historical Topo) is therefore misplaced by the datum shift, roughly 100 m at SF.

There is no test with a non-WGS84 GCS. NAD83 US Topo is unaffected (about 1 m). High is fair for a plausible field case.

I reran the fit with my own Snyder forward (verify/d6/aff.py) using the real USGS GPTS/LPTS:
- page→UTM 10N affine residual: 0.221 m at each of the 4 controls.
- page→lat/lon affine (what both platforms build: GeoPDFReader.swift:339-354, GeoPdfParser.kt → MapScreenHelpers.kt:495-497): 7.92 m RMS at the controls.
- Interior error against the UTM truth: up to 6.25 m, mean 3.4 m.

The Adobe path has no RMS gate on either platform. This only bites once D6-01 is fixed, and it is visible at z17+ as a doubled grid.

Note that the error grows roughly with sheet extent squared, so 1:50k/1:100k Adobe sheets would be much worse than this 1:24k case. Medium is fair for 1:24k.

iOS parseLGIDictRaw never reads /Registration; grep finds no 'Registration' in GeoPDFReader.swift. It returns crop-only when /CTM is absent (:681-684), so bounds() falls through to nil or the known-sheet table and then the camera fallback.

Android extractLegacyLgiDict (GeoPdfParser.kt:289-313) prefers /Registration via registrationCorrespondences (:319-341) and only then uses the CTM.

A Registration-only LGIDict is therefore georeferenced on Android and misplaced on iOS. Files that carry both /Registration and /CTM work on both platforms, so this is an edge case: medium.

**Android.** It rejects /Rotate≠0 (MapScreenHelpers.kt:423-437). Its GeoPDF correspondences are raw user space (GeoPdfParser.kt:211-212, BBox values), but the PdfRenderer page size and render matrix are box-relative (PdfPageRenderer.kt:68-75; pdfium's display matrix maps the crop box to 0..w,0..h). PdfTiler.kt:200-209 (h-y flip) and PdfGroundLayer corners 0..pw/0..ph (CustomMapOverlays.kt:849-856) both assume origin (0,0). A non-zero MediaBox or CropBox origin therefore shifts the map by origin×scale.

**iOS: the auditor's claim that it 'accounts for the mediaBox origin' is wrong.** I probed macOS PDFKit with ctypes (verify/d6/probe.py) and found that drawWithBox:toContext: itself translates the box origin to (0,0) and applies /Rotate:
- MediaBox [100 100 700 500] with a square at user 150,150: drawing with no manual translate puts it at 55,55. Adding the rasteriser's translate(-minX,-minY) pushes it off-canvas.
- A /Rotate 90 page is drawn rotated.

So PDFOverlay.swift:137-138 and PDFTiler.swift:209-210 double-subtract a non-zero MediaBox origin, and rotated pages are drawn rotated against an unrotated affine and canvas. Both platforms are broken for these inputs, and no test covers either. These inputs are uncommon from real producers, so medium stands.

Confirmed: affine_fits.json has 2 exact cases on a 1000×800 page, and mgrs_samples.json has 4 points. SharedVectorsTests.swift:79-80 and SharedVectorsTest.kt:84 use a 1e-3° round-trip tolerance. There are no shared vectors for GeoPDF parsing, UTM, tile math, grid labels or density, or zoom ranges.

One inaccuracy: case 1 does include a small rotation/shear (b=2e-5, d=-3e-5), so 'no rotation' is wrong. There is still no y-flip, noisy or realistic-magnitude case.

I checked the UTM divergence claim (verify/d6/U.java vs my Snyder replica). The iOS vendored Snyder forward differs from NGA Java by 1–2 cm in northing for identical inputs. That can flip a truncated 1 m readout only for points within about 2 cm of a metre boundary, so the user-visible impact is rare.

This is a coverage gap rather than an independent defect; medium is the ceiling.

Current state confirmed:
- PDFPickerSmokeTests.swift:10-31 only opens and cancels the picker.
- ScreenshotTests.importSeededGeoPDF (:533-571) asserts only app.buttons["Map"], and testCaptureGeoPdf states the device location is the sheet centre, so the camera-centred fallback from D6-01 looks plausible.
- PdfImportSmokeTest builds a trivial page with no georeference.
- samples/README.md still instructs copying into app Documents, while ScreenshotTests notes that file sharing is disabled.

This is a test-plan item with no independent user-facing defect; its impact is the bugs it let through (D6-01/02/05/06). I rate it medium rather than high.

verify.missed:
**1. iOS mishandles non-zero MediaBox origins and /Rotate pages (not reported; D6-10 wrongly credits iOS with handling the origin).** Probed on macOS PDFKit with verify/d6/probe.py: page.draw(with: .mediaBox, to:) already maps the MediaBox origin to (0,0) and applies /Rotate.
- ios/TacticalMaps/Calibration/PDFOverlay.swift:137-138 (translateBy(-renderRect.minX, -renderRect.minY) followed by page.draw) and ios/TacticalMaps/Calibration/PDFTiler.swift:209-210 subtract the origin a second time.
- iOS has no /Rotate handling anywhere under ios/TacticalMaps/Calibration: no rotation reads, and no preflight equivalent to Android's MapScreenHelpers.kt:423-437.
- Result: a GeoPDF with MediaBox [100 150 …] is shifted by the origin times the map scale in both the live overlay and the baked tiles. A /Rotate 90 page is drawn rotated inside an unrotated canvas and against an unrotated affine, so the placement is garbage.

**2. The iOS grid rebuilds on nearly every pan frame (minor).** The %.3f° fingerprint at ios/TacticalMaps/Map/Renderer/TileMapContainer.swift:553-558 changes about every 0.7 pt at z10+, so its "avoids re-tessellating during small pans" comment does not hold at working zooms.
